NIG8769: Members of PENGASSAN protest over two days over a management issue.
NIG8772: One killed, several wounded in a Edo communal clash between those of Uneme and Okpella villages. The clash may have been related to access to a logging area.

NIG8766: Members of PENGASSAN protest over two days over a management issue.

NIG8723: Protest against persistent Fulani violence in Asaba on 09/02.

NIG8627: Members of the AYT protest in Lagos over a ruling of an appeal in regards to an election.

NIG8621: Supporters of IPOB protest in Enugu, calling for the release of a jailed leader, Nnamdi Kanu. Several arrests reported.
NIG8619: Residents near a University protest attacks by 'thugs' attempting to remove them from their land for the purposes of development. Details of the attacks protested not known.

NIG8616: Residents of the Ondo State Southern Senatorial District (in or around Okitipupa or Erinje town) protest prolonged power outages, several arrests reported. Date of the protest not known. No reports of arrests occurring during the actual protests.
NIG8617: Supporters of IPOB protest in Asaba, calling for the release of a jailed leader, Nnamdi Kanu.

NIG8609: Youths in Owo protest against 'indoctrinate arrests' in the town on 14/01.

NIG8601: Vigilantes kill four suspected thieves in Jinowu.

NIG7932: Boko Haram attacks Mainuk on 13/07, thirty causalities.

NIG7921: An unidentified suicide bomber kills four, plus himself, and injures three others along a highway in Maiduguri during the early morning hours.
NIG7926: Boko Haram suicide bombers target the Borno Express Terminus Motor Park, Maiduguri, killing two passer-by and injuring three others. The number of bombers killed in the explosion are not known.

NIG7919: Boko Haram (actor not confirmed) attack and kill a monarch and three others at Nkerefi in Nkanu East Local Government Area on 10/07.
NIG7920: An unidentified armed group attacks and kills a monarch and three others at Nkerefi in Nkanu East Local Government Area on 10/07.

NIG7905: Hundreds protest power outages in Igarra.

NIG7906: Employees of a hospital in Owerri protest for the removal of its chief medical officer over 'highhandedness' and 'inhuman policies.' Police forces were present at the protest.

NIG7899: Members of CAN protest the Boko Haram prisoner relocation to a nearby location.
NIG7898: Following an attack on a mosque on 05/07 a protesting group burns two churches.
NIG7902: Non-academic staff of Obafemi Awolowo University protest over non-payment of salaries in Ile-Ife.
NIG7897: Unidentified persons attacked and killed an Agip Oil manager. The reason for the attack is not known - the perpetrators took nothing off the victims person.

NIG7896: A suicide bomber killed himself, a pastor and four worshipers at a Potiskum church. No report of the bombers association.
NIG7892: Members of the NYSC protest unpaid allowances 'at the weekend' in Minna.
NIG7891: At least 55 people have been killed in a 04/07 attack by Boko Haram suicide bombers in Zabamari, Jere LGA, 6 miles from Maiduguri.

NIG7887: Members of the ASUU, Ambrose Alli University (AAU), Ekpoma Chapter took to the streets of the university town to protest the recent kidnap of their colleague.
NIG7883: Children protest in Yakurr against child marriage.
NIG7884: Boko Haram attacks Bama on 03/07. Causalities not known.

NIG7890: A prominent politician and businessman is shot and killed by unknown assailants.

NIG7873: Aviation workers protest at Murtala Mohammed International Airport after a member of their union was dismissed.
NIG7879: An APC candidate is abducted in Akwanga during the overnight hours.

NIG7870: Traders protest the destruction of their shops.
NIG7869: Traders in Ekwulobia on 30/06 protest a relocation of Boko Haram prisoners to their area.
NIG7868: Four are dead in a clash between Fulani and Berom in Barikin Ladi on 30/06. Date disputed: some sources claim 29/06, others 30/06.
NIG7867: A group of taxi drivers protest for the removal of a government traffic bureaucracy after a string a alleged abuses.

NIG7858: A violent taxi driver protest along Dei-Dei junction injures one. Date not known - source claims 'at the weekend.'

NIG7856: Youths block roads in Awka and Onitsha in protest of a plan to relocate Boko Haram prisoners to their area.

NIG7854: Some Ikorodu indigenes protested at the Lagos state secretariat protesting the selection of a political leader for their area on 25/06.
NIG7852: Taxi drivers barricade 'Kaduna-Abuja flyover,' Kaduna State in protest of alleged police harassment.
NIG7853: Police and army clash at Ngwa High School Forward Operation Base. The nature of the clash is believed to be related to the holding of military ID cards by police. NIG7845: Suspected assassins target and kill a leading doctor in Alakuko. The reason for the attack is not known.
NIG7848: A young girl carrying a suicide pack detonates at a crowded market in Wagur on 23/06, killing ten and injuring 30.

NIG7847: Protesters gather at the National Assembly over a proposed increase of lawmaker pay.

NIG7844: Two suspected robbers are attacked and set alight by a vigilante militia in Nkpor on 22/06.

NIG7843: Residents of Awada Obosi in Idemili North Local Government Area of Anambra State 22/06 took to streets to protest what they described as poor electricity supply and high bills.

NIG7836: Residents protest a private building development in Owerri 'at the weekend.'
NIG7837: Residents protest poor electricity supply in Onitsha 'at the weekend.'

NIG7831: Police avert a group of striking workers from attacking a group of labour scabs.
NIG7829: Assailants suspected to be Fulani herdsmen hacked to death eight farmers in Sondi village in Wukari district of Taraba State on 18/06.

NIG7824: A pair of suspected thieves are attacked and killed by mob justice in Nkpor.
NIG7818: Commercial motorbike operators protest a restriction on their movement in Awka on 16/05.

NIG7820: Residents protest poor water supply in the Onitsha suburb of Awada and in Ogidi.
NIG7822: Members of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP), Ondo State chapter, yesterday (16/06) staged a protest, demanding payment of their three months pension.

NIG7804: Patients at the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) protest increased medical costs 'at the weekend.'
NIG7805: Hawkers of sachet water in Aba have, 'at the weekend,' protested a hike in price of the product by the manufacturers.
NIG7806: Staff of the Nigerian Petroleum Development Company, NPDC attached to the Eriemu oil field, Ughelli North Local Government Area, Delta State, embarked on a protest against the alleged non-payment of their six months' salaries and bonuses.

NIG7792: Edo workers protest unpaid salaries in Benin City.

NIG7789: A group of woman protest, accusing local politicians of taking bribes in return for appointing desired monarchs.

NIG7769: Representatives of ex-Niger Delta militants protest the delay in payment of their allowances under an amnesty programme by the federal government on 03/06 in Abuja.

NIG7763: Unidentified gunmen early in the day killed a Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) youth leader in Ushongo LGA of Benue State.

NIG7546: Ijaw and Itsekiri militia clash late 13/04 and early 14/03 in Ugborodo. What sparked off the fighting was not immediately clear, but it was learnt that armed Ijaw youths burnt no fewer than three houses in the Madangho area. Several injuries reported, including machete cuts.
NIG7547: Ondo State Government House, Alagbaka, Akure turned to a battle field as supporters of the state Governor, and his deputy, engaged themselves in free for all over a contested defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). Police dispersed the rioters. The clash began as a protest. Injuries not known.
NIG7541: Over 200 supporters of Labour Party, 12/04 protested around the office of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, in Asaba over what they described as the malpractices that trailed the result of last Saturday gubernatorial and House of Assembly elections.
NIG7542: PDP and APC clash with weapons in election day related violence. Sporadic violence resurfaced the following day in several areas around the city. Three reported dead over the two days.
NIG7543: Election related violence reported in several Rivers State areas, including Gokana, Kana, Asari Toru, Ikwere, Obio Akpor, Ozuoba, Bomu, Norwa, among others (not listed). Details of events not known.
NIG7544: Non-violent activity: Suspected Ombatse militia (Eggon group) attack the Nasarawa State presidential lodge, shooting sporadically. Although the mission of the suspected gunmen is unknown, it is believed that the target may be the state governor, Tanko Al-Makura, who usually held unofficial engagements at the lodge, especially during the electioneering period - though it is not clear if he, or anyone else was present at the time of the attack. One of the suspects was beaten by youth after he was caught by security operatives who arrived the scene of the incident.
NIG7504: Political violence reported in Okitipupa. Details scarce: Reported - 'political thugs' had a 'free day.'
NIG7503: Political violence reported in Ode-Aye. Details scarce: Reported - 'political thugs' had a 'free day.'
NIG7505: In Ore, Odigbo local government area, 'hoodlums' took over the major streets, shooting harassing and intimidating voters and INEC staff. The thugs stormed the house of a prominent politician in the town, manhandled him and set ablaze his car, while his family members fled.
NIG7506: 'Political thugs' fired sporadically, ambushing INEC staff in Ugbo on the day of a state election.
NIG7510: A PDP chairman is assassinated by unknown gunmen in Ezza-Agu.
NIG7513: PDP 'thugs' attack election officials and steal election materials in Dan Musa. Two reportedly shot - fatalities, injuries not known.
NIG7520: 'Thugs', suspected to be sympathetic to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the early hours of 11/04 attacked some supporters of the All Progressive Congress(APC) at Itchi polling unit in Igbo Eze South Local Government Area. The attackers may have been 'supervised' by police.
NIG7521: A reporter and his photographer were attacked and beaten by angry youths in Rumu-Osi. The details of the attack were not clear.
NIG7527: Military forces kill four voters (likely APC) in Bayan Dutse. Witness claim: 'The soldiers opened fire on the voters who challenged them from arresting the elders.'
NIG7528: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill an APC youth leader in Idu community.
NIG7535: Election related violence from a PDP supporter leaves a Psychology student dead in Makurdi.
NIG7536: Five are reportedly killed in election violence in several Akwa Ibom locations, including Mbiabong Etoi, Shelter Afrique in Uyo; Ndiya in Nsit Ubium; Etim Ekpo, and Ini Local Government Areas of the state. The number and location of each death is not known, with the exception of Uyo, where two are dead following a clash. It is not clear if the nature of the violence in the remaining areas were a clash or VOC - details limited.
NIG7540: A PDP councillor on election duty is beaten to death in Bogoro. Perpetrators not identified.
NIG7509: Police shoot and kill a man wielding a knife in an effort to break up a election-related scuffle in Jos North.
NIG7515: A police officer is 'hacked to death' in the Borokiri area of Port Harcourt, reasons unknown.
NIG7496: On 11 April 2015, the Directorate of State Security operatives and police personnel have clashed at the Independent National Electoral Commissions (INEC) headquarters in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The reason for the clash was not reported by the source. No fatalities reported
NIG7512: A group of voters attacked soldiers at a polling area in Tukurwa with stones. The soldiers responded in kind. Several reported arrests.
NIG7519: Soldiers allegedly shot dead three people in Suru local government of Kebbi State (exact location not know) after pandemonium broke out during the polls.
NIG7529: Fracas broke out at State Primary School, Olanada Rumuola, where some persons had attempted to snatch sensitive electoral materials. This was followed by a prolonged altercation which resulted in the destruction of electoral materials and manhandling of a police officer.
NIG7511: Youths protest a faulty voter card reader in Somolu.
NIG7508: At least two youths dead and many others severely injured in Warri during the governorship and House of Assembly polls as PDP factions clashed with the opposition All Progressives Congress, APC.
NIG7495: A crowd of some 2,000 protesters delayed distribution of materials in the state capital Port Harcourt, causing the ballots to open hours later than planned. The cause of the protest is not known.
NIG7507: APC and PDP members clash during state elections. Several machete cuts reported.
NIG7514: PDP and APC clash with weapons in election day related violence. Sporadic violence resurfaced the following day in several areas around the city. Three reported dead over the two days.
NIG7516: On 11 April 2015, an unidentified armed group clashed with a local youth militia when they attacked an INEC polling station on the Ikot Epene road in Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom). 2 youths shot and killed. 2 fatalities reported
NIG7517: Witnesses reported 'heavy shootings' in Buguma, preceding the election. The violence spilled over into the following day with supporters of several parties blocking roads with burning tyres.
NIG7518: Voters in Garaku protest the late arrival of election materials to their area.
NIG7525: Election related violence reported in several Rivers State areas, including Gokana, Kana, Asari Toru, Ikwere, Obio Akpor, Ozuoba, Bomu, Norwa, among others (not listed). Details of events not known.
NIG7530: An attempt to snatch election materials in Rumu-Osi (Rumuomasi) resulted in a clash between party agents (not identified).
NIG7490: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill five persons, steal election material in Buguma. A government officials home was also torched.
NIG7481: An APC supporter is killed in Garki, Jigawa state allegedly by supporters of the People Democratic Party (PDP). The police spokesperson in the state DSP Abdul Jinjiri Confirmed the incident to news men adding that three people were arrested in connection. The attack occurred on the 'eve of [the states] gubernatorial election,' or 10/04.
NIG7482: A close ally of the PDP deputy governorship candidate was shot dead in his in Ikwo local council area by suspected Labour Party gunmen on 10/04.
NIG7483: Five members of the PDP were abducted by suspected pirates along the Brass waterway in Brass, Brass LGA. The PDP members were travelling to Twon-Brass to participate in the election the following day.
NIG7484: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill two Lokoja-based missionaries at Emiguni emidojo village in Bassa Local Government Areas. The reason for the attack is not known. Date not known - source dated 10/04.
NIG7487: Military forces have recaptured Bita, Izge Yamteke and Uba towns in Askira Uba and Damboa local council areas of Borno State following a battle that included the aid of air forces. An array of weapons were recovered from fleeing Boko Haram. Casualties, fatalities not known.
NIG7489: The River State governor is nearly attacked by 'irate youths' when he stopped over at Omagwu, reason unknown. The governor was barricaded by his security personnel shortly afterward.
NIG7492: A group of heavily armed men attack Ilase (Ilashe) the morning of 10/04, but were repelled by police forces. One civilian is believed to have been shot, fate unknown.
NIG7480: Military forces recapture four towns (not named) from Boko Haram in the Sambisa forest region. Two are killed when a group of 20 unidentified gunmen attacked Eku village, Ethiope East. The operation is believed to have begun on 09/04, possibly before.
NIG7491: Some serving members of the National Youth Corp Service (NYSC) stage a peaceful protest to demand of their allowances for the functions they carried out during the March 28th Presidential and National Assembly elections in Cross River State.
NIG7493: Youths protest the non-availability of election materials or results in Oko Ita.
NIG7494: Commercial tricycle, Keke NAPEP, operators protest the killing of one their colleagues, who have disappeared earlier in the week.
NIG7477: Boko Haram attacks Dille village at 2am, killing 20 residents and burning houses.
NIG7476: Suspected Boko Haram insurgents attacked Buratai village in Biu local government area of Borno State where they killed two people and injured three others.
NIG7479: Unidentified gunmen attack Fulanis, killing two and injuring one in Buruku.
NIG7478: Military forces begin an operation to rid Boko Haram from several location in the Sambisa forest region on 09/04, locations not provided. Military forces captured four locations on 10/04. 'Scores' of Boko Haram killed, with at least one soldier KIA.
NIG7474: Importers protest at a Apapa headquarters of a shipping company over their refusal to grant the proper bureaucratic materials that would allow their shipments. The protesters numbered 1,000.
NIG7475: On 9 April 2015, some members Academic staff of the University of Calabar protest non-payment of their ad-hoc services at the office of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River).
NIG7472: Unidentified, mask-wearing gunmen attack and kill 9 Fulani men Rigacikun. The attack occurred 'last week.'
NIG7473: Unidentified gunmen abduct 30 Fulani men at a market in Sabon Birni. The kidnapping occurred 'last week.'
NIG7471: Two are killed when a group of 20 unidentified gunmen attacked Eku village, Ethiope East. Additionally, a unnumbered group of NYSC were abducted by the gunmen. Perpetrators not known.
NIG7464: Traders protest a shop-sharing proposal at the Sapele Local Government Council and Sapele Police Station.
NIG7467: A group of Igbo youths protest the outcome of the 28/03 election in Awka, Onitsha, Ekwolobia, Agulu and Nnewi. The protesters blamed the PDP for vote-rigging.
NIG7470: PDP supporters protest alleged plots by the All Progressives Congress, APC, to use the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to manipulate the forthcoming governorship and state House of Assembly elections in the state.
NIG7460: A middle-aged man was killed in Efon Alaaye Ekiti, headquarters as members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) staged violent protests against the plot by 19 All Progressives Congress (APC) lawmakers to impeach Governor Ayodele Fayose. NIG7462: Military forces recapture Boko Haram camps in Alagarno following a raid. Military forces report 'huge' Boko Haram losses - no numbers provided.
NIG7458: Igbo youth groups demonstrated in 'Anambra State' (location not reported) to protest the alleged rigging of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), during the presidential and national assembly elections in the state.
NIG7459: Protesters from Rivers State have demonstrators at the INEC headquarters in Abuja, demanding the removal of the states Resident Electoral Commissioner, alleging vote rigging and fraud.
NIG7461: A group of APC lawmakers and supporters ram a barricade erected by the PDP at Ita Ore in protest of a move to impeach the governor. The riot caused one death in nearby Efon-Alaiye. The lawmakers were on their way to Ado-Ekiti to vote on the measure, but were eventually stopped by soldiers.
NIG7463: Women of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA staged a peaceful protest against alleged voter fraud by the PDP.
NIG7457: Unidentified gunmen open fire on a group of traders in Sabon Birnin during the afternoon hours, killing 14 and injuring several others.
NIG7455: A mob attacked the residence of Katsina State Governorship candidate of All Progressive Congress (APC) and vandalised parts of the buildings and five vehicles parked at the premises. An eyewitness told our reporter that the mob stormed the area with sticks and cutlasses which they used in the act. The exact location of the attack is not known, though the politician represents Malumfashi. No reported injuries.
NIG7456: Ten believed killed in a clash between groups of hunters and cattle rustlers (both unidentified) over a land issue in Shimfida. Date not known - source dated 06/04.
NIG7453: Numbering 20, Boko Haram, disguised as preachers, attack and killed 24 who were observing sunset prayers in Kwajaffa Babur.
NIG7454: On 5 April 2015, residents stopped and killed a suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber attempting to enter a mosque in Biu city (Borno). Another suspected bomber was also assaulted by another group of locals at a second location in the city.
NIG7451: Four traders are dead when 'scores' of Boko Haram attacked a market in Kayamla village (near Konduga) during the mid-afternoon. Following the attack a group of vigilantes from Konduga mobilised, but the attackers had fled before they had arrived. A similar attack occurred the previous day in nearby Alau.
NIG7452: Unknown gunmen on the night of 04/04 reportedly assassinated a prominent chief in Egbada in Ogba Egbema Ndoni local government area of Rivers State.
NIG7440: Unidentified gunmen stormed two communities of Rivers State, Obrikom and Obor, killing at least nine people and injuring two others.
NIG7443: Four fishermen were beheaded and dumped inside the river Alau by suspected Boko Haram on 03/03. After - and separate even- a group of Civilian JTF chased the attackers to a nearby Balle village (not named), where they killed at least one perpetrator.
NIG7444: Unidentified gunmen attack supporters of APC, including the home of a candidate for the local government area in Obrikom and Obior, killing six (one source counts seven). The politicians home was believe to be Obrikom.
NIG7446: Security forces kill 'dozens' of Boko Haram in Alagarno, while routing them from several villages (Yajiwa, Afa, Kafa and Maudori) in Damboa LGA. The numbers of wounded and dead from the smaller, surrounding villages are not known. Included in the operation were aircraft strikes and heavy artillery.
NIG7442: Four fishermen are beheaded and dumped inside the river Alau (in Konduga) by suspected Boko Haram on 03/03. A group of Civilian JTF chased the attackers to a nearby Balle village (not named), where they killed at least one perpetrator.
NIG7435: An explosion in the early evening near a bus station in the northeast city of Gombe killed ten and injured several others. The attack had the 'hallmarks' of Boko Haram and witnesses described the attack as the work of a female suicide bomber.
NIG7439: Fulani gunmen attack the villages of Kurungu, Tse Vir, Abur and Agberga in which no fewer than 30 persons were killed.
NIG7432: Arsonists destroy a church housing building at Gidan Maso village in Rogo Local Government Area, killing the pastors daughter. It is believed the target of the attackers was a person who had converted to Christianity from Islam.
NIG7433: Unidentified gunmen, identified only as 'militants,' kidnap five Exxon Mobil workers in Qua Iboe Terminal Ibeno. The kidnapping may be related to the recent election.
NIG7434: Suspected 'party thugs' attack the All Progressives Congress (APC) secretariat in Ado-Ekiti, assaulting its members. The attackers were not identified.
NIG7431: Nine Chadian soldiers were killed and 16 wounded after being ambushed by Boko Haram fighters in Malam Fatori.
NIG7429: Members of the PDP protest the election returns of several states in Abuja.
NIG7430: A group of youths protest a delay in the release of election results in Umuahia.
NIG7423: Youths block the entrance to an election collection centre in South Jos in protest of the current governors declaration of victory. Security operatives dispersed the protesters.
NIG7415: Four Boko Haram combatants are killed in a clash with military forces in Gombe Aba.
NIG7417: A group of APC women protest against the 'conduct of elections' in Rivers State. The demonstrators were dispersed with police tear-gas when they attempted to register their complaints with officials. No reported injury.
NIG7424: Military forces repel a Boko Haram attack on Dukku, at least one captured. Recovered from Boko Haram was include a Hilux van, a smart card reader machine belonging to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and three boxes of assorted ammunition, among other items.
NIG7425: Residents protest election results in Calabar.
NIG7416: On 30 March 2015, members of Boko Haram clashed with and killed three members of a local armed group from Tafawa-Balewa in Jitar (Bauchi, Bauchi).
NIG7418: Supporters of the PMDC protest an election result in Enugu.
NIG7419: On 30 March 2015, Boko Haram members clashed with a local armed group in Tafawa-Balewa (Tafawa-Balewa, Bauchi) during the morning hours, shooting sporadically. The attackers were pushed back by the armed group, who killed four. The vigilantes pursued them to Jitar.
NIG7420: 5,000 members of the NYSC protest non-payment of their training and logistic allowances for the ongoing elections along the Asaba/Onitsha Highway in Oshimili South.
NIG7421: PDP members protest the destruction of political billboards in Saminaka. The billboards were believed to have been destroyed by an area street gang known as the 'Area Boys.' Date of the protest is not known, source dated 30/03.
NIG7422: Members of several political parties protest 'voting irregularities' and demanded the cancellation of its results.
NIG7426: Chieftains and supporters of All Progressive Congress (APC) staged a peaceful protest in Uyo calling for the cancellation of the Presidential and National Assembly elections in the state. NIG7427: 'Thugs' storm a Yenagoa court room in an apparent attempt to force a judge to make a favourable ruling on a case concerning the PDP.
NIG7428: Property destruction: Suspected arsonists set ablaze the Isiokolo office of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC damaging files and other sensitive items within the building. The fire is believed to be related to the recent election.
NIG7409: Soldiers shot and killed a member of the Islamic Movement of Nigeria. It is not clear if the victim was shot due to his political affiliations.
NIG7412: Believed fleeing a battle in Dungulbi, a member of Boko Haram shoots and kills a civilian man in nearby Bishi.
NIG7406: Chadian and Nigerian forces overtake Badam (Abadam) from Boko Haram, kill 50.
NIG7407: On 29 March 2015, an unidentified armed group attacked Alkaleri and Kirfi, coded separately, Alkaleri ( Alkaleri, Bauchi). NIG7410: Nigerian forces battle 'scores' of Boko Haram fighters outside Bauchi, in the town of Dungulbi. The ground attack was aided by air support. Military sources claim Boko Haram has suffered 'serious losses' during the operation.
NIG7414: Thousands of APC party members in Port Harcourt protested against the handling of the Presidential and National Assembly elections held [on 28/03] in Rivers State. Police were present at the protest.
NIG7405: Protest in Aba over delayed election results.
NIG7411: Property destruction: On 29 March 2015, some ISWAP militants attacked an INEC polling station in Bauchi (Bauchi, Bauchi) and destroyed some ballot boxes.
NIG7413: Rioting youths attacked a private radio station, Unity FM, as well as a group of journalists who were present. The youths were after a PDP chieftain for making an inciting statement on live programme on radio. The youths threw stones, damaged five cars and injured a youth leader from Zinaria community who tried to calm them.
NIG7396: An unidentified youth is shot near the home of the state Commissioner for Social Welfare. The attack may have a connection to national elections being presently held.
NIG7381: On 28 March 2015, ISWAP militants attacked an INEC polling station in the villages of Bir Balawa (Nafada, Gombe) and Biri Filani, coded separately. They opened fire on voters at the station. One person died during the attack in Birin Bolawa, and another died in Birin Fulani. 1 fatality was reported
NIG7383: On 28 March 2015, ISWAP militants attacked an INEC polling station in Dukku (Dukku, Gombe) and shot voters queued up at polling stations. The attackers killed three and injured two others. NIG7384: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attack the outskirts of Nafada in an attempt to disrupt ongoing elections. Casualties not known.
NIG7385: Gunmen believed to be of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) attack the home of Lagos state Commissioner for Transportation injuring at least one person. NIG7391: On 28 March 2015, an unidentified armed group attacked an INEC ad-hoc staff in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). No further details
NIG7392: A Youth leader of the APC was allegedly killed by suspected hoodlums in Obagienevbosa Community, Ikpoba Okha Local Government Area of Edo State during Saturdays Presidential and National Assembly elections. NIG7393: 'Angry youths' pelt a prominent PDP member and potential office holders car with stones, causing the candidate to flee a polling area.
NIG7394: Boko Haram gunmen open fire on residents of Miringa, killing 25. The killing may be in relation the election. The attack occurred early in the day.
NIG7397: An unidentified young male voter was killed at Ward 3, Unit 2 in Eleme Local Government Area of the state. Perpetrators not known. The political attitudes of the victim are not known.
NIG7402: On 28 March 2015, an IED planted by an unidentified armed group detonated at an INEC Polling Station in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Causalities/injuries not known.
NIG7403: A man who had recently defected from the APC to the PDP is murdered in Ikirun the morning of 28/03.
NIG7404: Two PDP politicians were attacked by a mob during accreditation. One of the politicians aids were injured in the melee. Perpetrators not known.
NIG7386: Defusal: An explosive device is discovered outside a government building on the morning of 28/03. NIG7387: An IED is discovered in front of a government house in Osisioma during the morning hours. NIG7395: A soldier is killed while on election security duty by unknown persons. The attack took place at the in the Whimpy area of Abio/Akpor Local Government Area.
NIG7388: Thousands of placard carrying indigenes, mostly widows in the Nne-Ogidi village Agulu in the Anaocha Local Government Area of Anambra State 'at the weekend' protested what they tagged forceful possession of their lands by a man (name withheld) in the community.
NIG7389: Violence reported between APC and PDP members on election day. Shots were believed to have been fired and a government building set ablaze. Injuries/fatalities not known.

NIG7399: Election day violence reported between PDP and APC supporters in Ikirun. Unknown causalities. It is not clear if the clash had any relationship between the killing of a man who had defected from the APC to the PDP earlier in the morning.
NIG7401: Election day violence reported between members of the APC and PDP in Olomu. One death reported.
NIG7378: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen beheaded 23 people, injure 32 others and set fire to homes in Buratai. The attack come on the eve of an election, which Abubakar Shekau had vowed to disrupt.
NIG7377: Military forces retake Gwoza while killing several members of Boko Haram and capturing several others. Numbers not provided.
NIG7379: Three persons were confirmed dead in a clash between supporters of People Democratic Party [PDP] and the loyalists of All Progressive Congress [APC] in Rivers State - location and battle details not known.

NIG7375: Airline passengers protest frequent flight delays.
NIG7376: Governor Rotimi Amaechi (APC) of Rivers States convoy is attacked by 'political thugs' from 'from an opposition party'. The attackers fired live bullets at the convoy and there were two reports of injuries from the governors staff.
NIG7372: Nigerien and Chadian forces overtake Gachagar from Boko Haram following (at minimum) a two day air and ground bombardment. There have been skirmishes between the military and Boko Haram throughout the campaign Causality details not provided.
NIG7373: Factions of two rival political parties (affiliations unknown) clash over the closure of a market. By the time police restored order, eight people were seriously injured.
NIG7374: Staff of Lagos State University (LASU) continue a protest against the vice chancellor over several days.

NIG7363: Nigerien and Chadian forces overtake Gachagar from Boko Haram following (at minimum) a two day air and ground bombardment. There have been skirmishes between the military and Boko Haram throughout the campaign Causality details not provided.

NIG7366: Numbering 5,000 in total, members of the APC hold two simultaneous election rallies for their presidential candidate, Muhammadu Buhari.
NIG7364: Staff of Lagos State University (LASU) continue a protest against the vice chancellor over several days.
NIG7365: Factionist supporters of the OPC engage in running battles over what is believed to be the organization of a rally. Some rioters destroyed property, while others robbed members of the public. Several injuries reported.
NIG7368: On 25 March 2015, hundreds of PDP members in Ogun State protested the non-issuance of their Permanent Voters Cards at the headquarters of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun).
NIG7369: Youths protest an alleged diversion of water hyacinth jobs by the government.
NIG7358: Nigerien and Chadian forces overtake Gachagar from Boko Haram following (at minimum) a two day air and ground bombardment. There have been skirmishes between the military and Boko Haram throughout the campaign Causality details not provided.
NIG7359: Staff of Lagos State University (LASU) continue a protest against the vice chancellor over several days.
NIG7360: Members of the Benin branch of the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) matched through some major streets in Benin City, protesting the three-month old strike of the Edo State judicial workers.
NIG7361: Skirmishes between APC and PDP youths occur over two days in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA. First, on the evening of 23/03 in Okwuzi and on 24/03 in Omoku. Several building were reportedly destroyed.
NIG7362: Members of the Nigeria Labour Congrees group protests against a newly appointed president of the organization. Date of the protest vague. Source dated 24/03.
NIG7355: Gunmen suspected to be Fulani herdsmen killed five persons and injured many others during an attack on Ananum village in Donga Local Government Area of Taraba State. The victims are believed to be mainly Tiv.
NIG7351: Alleging disenfranchisement, a large number of voters protest in several areas of Afijio LGA. The protesters demanded voter cards, which have not yet been delivered. NIG7354: Staff of Lagos State University (LASU) continue a protest against the vice chancellor over several days.
NIG7356: Protesters called for the removal of the provost of a local college. Though leaders of several communities were involved, it is believed the protest took place only in Ekiadolor. It is not clear if the protesters were students of the institution.
NIG7357: Skirmishes between APC and PDP youths occur over two days in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni LGA. First, on the evening of 23/03 in Okwuzi and on 24/03 in Omoku. Several building were reportedly destroyed.

NIG7344: Staff of Lagos State University (LASU) continue a protest against the vice chancellor over several days.

NIG7343: A man believed to be an APC member is 'feared dead' after an attack by unidentified gunmen. Date not known - source dated 21/03.

NIG7284: Cameroonian forces clash with Boko Haram over two days in Ndaba, a Nigerian border town. Causalities not known.
NIG7288: Numbering 2,000, Sapele residents protest prolonged power outages in their area.

NIG7269: A group of mothers protest for the release of their children after their arrest following a violent riot.

NIG7244: Fulani gunmen attack Jootar over four days (07/03 - 10/03), causing five deaths and displacement of several persons.

NIG7248: Nine are dead in in Barkin Ladi, in a tit-for-tat attack against civilians of the two groups, which began against Fulanis.

NIG7241: Residents of Oteri protest a recent murder in their community and called on police to investigate more thoroughly.

NIG7237: gunmen attack Jootar over four days (07/03 - 10/03), causing five deaths and displacement of several persons.

NIG7165: Rival members of NURTW, vying for control of Oshodi, again clash in the city over two consecutive days. Five reported dead on the second day (25/02).
NIG7164: Protesters gather at the National Assembly complex to demand the passage of a law to prohibit possession of illegal fire arms.
NIG7162: Doctors at a Lagos State teaching hospital protest non-payment of their salaries in Idi-Araba.
NIG7161: A confederation of labour contractors protest non-payment of work completed.

NIG7167: Fifteen are reported dead and 50+ injuries after a suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber targeted a bus park in Potiskum. This was the second such attack in a week.
NIG7168: After suicide attacks in Kanot, it was reported that two suspects were attacked and set alight by angered youths in the area, though officials deny the vigilante attack.
NIG7163: Chadian military forces claim to have killed 207 Boko Haram fighters during fighting on 24/02. Additionally, one Chadian soldier was killed and another nine were wounded.
NIG7169: Military forces clash with Boko Haram at Gonori near Gamboru. Causalities not known.
NIG7160: Aggrieved members of the PDP protested in Onitsha against what they described as 'imposition of incapacitated and medically unfit candidate on them by the party.'
NIG7158: Residents of Ugbiyoko, a community in Egor Local Government Area of Edo State, protested at the headquarters of the Benin Electricity Distribution Company (in Benin) protesting against prolonged power outage in the area.

NIG7159: Unidentified persons attack the motorcade of APC governor candidate Simon Lalong in Jos East, destroying four vehicles. No report of injury.
NIG7155: Five masked gunmen kidnap an American missionary from a school in Emiworo, Kogi State. She was later released the given to American authorities in the area (Agence France Presse - source dated 07/03).
NIG7157: An eyewitness reports Boko Haram have destroyed Musa village at some point following the military offensive on location in Sambisa Forest - specific date not given, source dated 23/02. No reported of injuries or the targeting of individuals.
NIG7153: Property destruction: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) secretariat in Obi LGA of Nasarawa State was set ablaze early in the day by unknown persons. No reported injury.

NIG7132: Gunmen attack Ladi-Shehuri, where they killed and burned a man in his car.
NIG7133: Boko Haram attack two locations near Chinok, Lehu and Makalawa, 11 dead.

NIG7129: Supporters of the PDP and Labour Party clash for unknown reason in Ibadan, several injuries reported.
NIG7126: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attacked the Tamsu-Shehuri village on the night of 18/02, killing more than 12 people. Following the attack the perpetrators looted several homes taking food items.
NIG7127: Unidentified gunmen attacked and killed the deputy Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party of Sop Ward, Riyom Local Government Area, Plateau state and injured his daughter.

NIG7120: Customers of the Eko Electricity Distribution Company protest persistent power outages.
NIG7117: Suspected Boko Haram suicide bombers attack a restaurant in Potiskum, at least 3 dead, plus injuries.
NIG7118: Unidentified gunmen attack Mongul village, Kantoma district in Mangu Local Government Area and Gana-rop (Marik) villages of Barkinladi Local Government Area killing three. The reasons for the attacks are not known.

NIG7122: Unidentified attackers disrupt a APC campaign rally in Okrika with bombs and gunfire. Several APC leaders were present at the rally; one reported death, 50 injuries. Several people at the rally publicly blamed the PDP, though the party denies any involvement.
NIG7123: Boko Haram attacks Dang village the morning of 17/02, 10 dead.
NIG7124: Boko Haram attacks Faa village the morning of 17/02, 17 dead.
NIG7125: Suspected Boko Haram suicide bombers attack a police post in Yamarkumi, near Biu. 36 dead, 20 injured. Most of the victims were child vendors and street pan-handlers that usually crowd the checkpoint
NIG7114: Supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Adamawa Central Senatorial Zone, staged a peaceful protest over the arrest of the parties senatorial candidate in the area, which they believe was politically motivated.
NIG7113: Unidentified gunmen assassinate the Barkin Ladi chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the Kurra Drong area of Jos South, LGA during the early morning hours.
NIG7116: Boko Haram attacks the palace Emir of Askira in Askira-Uba on the evening of 15/02, burning the building to the ground before being driven into retreat by a local militia known as Jubrin Gunda. NIG7115: Suspected PDP supporters disrupt an APC campaign rally by blocking traffic. Police removed the protesters with tear gas.
NIG7105: Military forces report killing 300 members of Boko Haram over two days of fighting in several Borno locations, including: Monguno, Gabchari, Abba Jabari, Zuntur, Gajigana, Gajiram, Damakar, Kumaliwa, Bosso Wanti, Jeram and Kabrisungul. NIG7103: Boko Haram attacks the palace Emir of Askira in Askira-Uba on the evening of 15/02, burning the building to the ground before being driven into retreat by a local militia known as Jubrin Gunda. NIG7093: A suspected female Boko Haram suicide bomber attacked a bus station in Damaturu. At least 13 dead, 32 others injured.
NIG7102: Military forces report killing 300 members of Boko Haram over two days of fighting in several Borno locations, including: Monguno, Gabchari, Abba Jabari, Zuntur, Gajigana, Gajiram, Damakar, Kumaliwa, Bosso Wanti, Jeram and Kabrisungul. NIG7092: Hundreds of protesters in Abuja demonstrated against the planned removal of the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Prof. Attahiru Jega and further shift in new dates of the 2015 elections.
NIG7088: APC supporters block a road during the early hours of the day in protest of a theft at a leaders office, accusing the PDP of the crime. In reaction, PDP supporters mobilise a counter protest. Violence is narrowly avoided, police separated the two groups.

NIG7089: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill a Ogoni student unionist in Bori. Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) condemned the attack.

NIG7083: Students of a technical college protest, destroy property. The reason for the protest was not reported. Following the disturbances the school was closed indefinitely.
NIG7080: Members of the Ekrokpe community peacefully protest PDP-government neglect of bad roads. Exact date unknown - source dated 12/02.

NIG7082: A group of five unidentified gunmen attack a police station, killing two officers.

NIG7073: One person was feared dead while two were abducted in a clash between Ijaw community of Ezebiri and their Urhobo counterpart at Furukama in Bomadi and Ughelli South Local Government Areas of Delta State.
NIG7068: A police officer shot and killed a 10-year old girl and injured a woman at Kwani Mani police checkpoint in Bichi LGA for unknown reason. Date not known. Source dated 11/02.

NIG7077: A group suspected to be members of the Movement for the Actualization of Sovereign State of Biafra, MASSOB, invaded Onitsha main market, beating up traders who were protesting against a market levy.

NIG7067: Placard carrying secondary school teachers stormed Government House, Bauchi State to protest unpaid salaries.
NIG7061: Christian and Muslims clash in Babale, Jos North after a Muslim group attempted to fill in a large automobile accident causing ditch in a road - deeper reasons not known. Four killed, property destroyed.
NIG7065: Fulani attackers lay siege to two Benue State locations, killing five in each location and destroying property.
NIG7060: A group of militants attacked a group of protesting widows, seriously injuring five. The group was protesting Minister of State for Education who they believe was instrumental to the death of her husband.
NIG7063: A group of seven suspected murderers are captured and burned alive by a vigilante group in Naka.
NIG7062: Defusal: Military forces discover and demobilize 147 Boko Haram bombs in Auno, on the outskirts of Maiduguri.
NIG7066: Members of the BVYG, or civilian JTF, clash with police in Maiduguri over payment for hired protection of a political group. Injuries not known.
NIG7058: Pro-Jonathan protesters gather at the office at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to protest for greater distribution of voter cards.

NIG7053: Boko Haram stops a bus near Akada-Banga village of Bama district and abducted about 20 people, including women and children.

NIG7055: Boko Haram attacks a military barracks in Geidam (Gaida) on 08/02. Heavy fighting reported. Casualties not known.
NIG7052: Coalition of Concerned Nigerians, a social-human rights group based in Jos staged protest at INEC headquarters Abuja demanding that the elections be held as scheduled.
NIG7051: Fulani gunmen abduct the father of the former governor in Bokkos LGA. He was later rescued.
NIG7048: At least 10 persons were seriously injured and properties worth millions of naira were destroyed when soldiers from Orerokpe Community in Okpe Local Government Area, Delta State invaded neighbouring Omoise-Ovu Community in Ethiope East Local Government Area of Delta State on 07/02. NIG7042: Gunmen shoot and kill a Bauchi state lawmaker during the early morning hours. The perpetrators may have been kidnappers.

NIG6461: Players of a Kaduna-based football team protest the government over non-payment of salaries.
NIG6460: Urhobo youths, under the aegis of Coalition of Urhobo Youth Organisation, CUYO staged a peaceful protest at the Delta State Government House against what they described as the victimisation of Urhobo candidates who applied for the position Vice Chancellor of the Delta State University.

NIG6458: A group of Eggon youth attack a Nasarawa Eggon village and burned a house belonging to a relative of the state chairman, who may have been Fulani - motivation not known. Injuries not reported.
NIG6457: Agreement: Ten Boko Haram commanders surrender to military forces at Kawuri. Their capitulation comes days following reports Abubakar Shekau was found KIA.
NIG6456: Unidentified gunmen attack a Kogi police station at Adogo, stealing weapons and a armoured vehicle. No causalities or injuries reported. Police later reported the attack had been foiled by their forces.
NIG6455: Dressed as customers, suspected Boko Haram attack a market in Monguno, killing 9 and injuring 10. The attack occurred 'at the weekend.'
NIG6454: A vigilante group lynches three suspected kidnappers.
NIG6453: Fighters from Boko Haram stormed the northeastern town of Mainok, attacking civilians, sparking a gun battle that killed at least 36 people and continued into the following day. Among the dead were civilians.
NIG6451: Police open fire and kill two vigilantes as they attempted to lynch a group of suspected armed robbers.
NIG6452: Gunmen wearing military uniforms attack Tadabale village, kill two people and steal cattle.
NIG22884: On 19 September 2014, a group of four men in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano) beat up a worker working on sexual orientation and gender identity issues. He was seriously injured and hospitalized for three days.
NIG6450: Fighters from Boko Haram stormed the northeastern town of Mainok, attacking civilians, sparking a gun battle that killed at least 36 people and continued into the following day. Among the dead were civilians.
NIG6447: Fulani gunmen ambush a group of soldiers on a patrol between Fadan Karshi (Fadan Kaibi) to Karshi Daji. One soldier killed, four injured. The gunmen split into three groups, one continuing into Fadan Kaibi, where they killed 12 villiagers, burnt down 20 houses and injured scores. Another group (or the same, later) went to Karshi Daji, killed 20 people and burnt down several houses. The third group attacked Unguwan Ganye, though casualties are not known.
NIG6444: Trader protest levies at Eke-Awka market.
NIG6439: Various groups protest a ban on Okada-motorcycle business in the area.
NIG6438: Boko Haram kill the Governor of Adamawas uncle during a raid on his Madagali residence. The attack was an apparent targeted assassination. Following the attack it was reported a Boko Haram commander was residing in the residence.
NIG6442: A group of villagers attempt to lynch a Nigerien national on the suspicion of involvement in an alleged ritual murder of a young girl. The police intervened, however, drawing ire from the larger community, many of whom later attacked the police station. Four rioters were killed when the police launched a defence, 89 arrested.
NIG6445: Two suicide bombers and a gunmen enter a university campus, kill 15. Boko Haram was later blamed for the attack. Among the dead were the two suicide bombers.
NIG6437: Military forces fight through a Boko Haram ambush, capture a senior leader, identity unknown. One soldier was reported dead after the battle.
NIG6440: Following an extensive battle the previous day, Boko Haram again returns to Konduga (presumably to retrieve their dead) and is engaged into another battle. Sixty reported Boko Haram deaths, military forces wound and kill a notable commander, later revealed to be Abubakar Shekau, though Shekau may have been captured in nearby Benisheikh. A matter of dispute: some believe this may have been a been a body double. It was gathered that when the militants discovered that Konduga was a no go area, they headed to nearby Benisheikh and laid ambush for troops on patrol duties.
NIG6443: Boko Haram attempts to take over the Kano-Maiduguri highway in Ngamdu, and are dramatically pushed back by military forces who report to have killed 150 or more in the ensuing battle.
NIG6436: 30 women in the Watt Market, Calabar protest at the Cross River house assembly over what they describe as double taxation by the state government.
NIG6434: Boko Haram again attempts to overtake Konduga. Military forces retaliate, killing an estimated 100. The battle is believed to have lasted over twelve hours.
NIG6435: Two Boko Haram commanders and 15 of their fighters are killed in a pair of clashes with military forces in Baaza and Michika.
NIG6432: A group of ex-militants protest in Bomadi over the proposed creation of a lopsided number of polling units in their area campared to other areas of the country.
NIG6431: 11,000 aggrieved pensioners of Power Holding Company of Nigeria (PHCN) embarked on peaceful protest to demand payment of their entitlements.
NIG6430: Students of Lagos State University (LASU) External System stormed the Governors Office, Alausa, Ikeja, in protest over various complaints, including high fees, extended academic calendar, delayed issuance of results, among others.
NIG6427: Fulani gunmen attack Mbar in Bokkos LGA killing five with machetes. The attack occurred during midday.
NIG6428: Boko Haram abducts a group of 50 women and children from Gulak. '[Boko Haram] started loading our women and children into their vehicles, threatening to shoot whoever disobeyed them. Everybody was scared,' a witness stated. The date of the attack was not included in the report, but is likely to have occurred on 13/09 or 14/09.
NIG6429: No fewer than twenty persons have been feared dead and scores of others injured when Fulani herdsmen allegedly invaded Tunari village in Wukari Local Government of Taraba State. The attackers were said to have stormed the village at 10 am and set houses ablaze while most residents were attending a church service.
NIG6426: Anglican Church leaders and petitioners protest the destruction of their church building.
NIG6424: Young people believed to be students of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, went on rampage as they protested power outage in Erifun community where many students of the institution are known to reside. The protesting students stoned the vehicle of legal luminary and also attempted to vandalise one of the hostels in Afe Babalola University. The violent protest also carried over into nearby Erifun.
NIG6425: Protesting students of Federal Polytechnic clash with police over power outages. Causalities, injuries not known.
NIG6421: PENGASSAN workers strike and protest at the Group Managing Director office in Abuja.
NIG6423: Boko Haram launches a 'massive' attack on Konduga, 35km from Maiduguri, causing a three-hour battle with military forces. Reports indicate Boko Haram suffered heavy causalities before fleeing. Military forces captured several pieces of heavy equipment and weapons from the attackers. Xinhua places the death number of Boko Haram at 100, others place it as high as 120. Later reports suggest the causality total with as high as 250, with four injured military. A air force jet was downed during the operation - the pilot was later captured by Boko Haram, who nearly a month later released a video of his beheading.
NIG6420: Workers of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado Ekiti, have staged a protest and called for the removal of the Rector of the institution after several employees salaries had been cut.
NIG6419: Retired soldiers, numbering 100, protested in Benin City over the non-payment of pensions. The group threatened guerrilla warfare if their demands were not met.
NIG6418: No fewer than 75 members of Boko Haram have reportedly been killed by local hunters in Michika and Madagali local government areas of Adamawa state. Date(s) unknown.
NIG6416: Retired military personnel protest over irregular pension payments in Abuja.
NIG6415: BringBackOurGirls supporters protest in Abuja for the removal of presidential aids.
NIG6414: Retirees of the Power Holding Company of Nigeria (PHCN), protested in Lagos against the non-payment of their accumulated pension benefits.
NIG6410: Retirees protest the non-payment of their pensions in Asaba.
NIG6409: An explosive went off at the Okaka Estate, Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, causing panic among the residents. Although nobody died, one person was reportedly injured.
NIG6413: A group of youth in the Ode-Ugborodo community attack a group of sailors during the early morning hours after ordering them to leave the area. Two injuries reported.
NIG6411: A riotous mob attacked the vigilante group (not identified) guarding the Main Market for allegedly killing a labourer over a SIM Card dispute.
NIG6412: Staff of Nigeria Export Processing Zones Authority (NEPZA) protested at the organisations headquarters in Abuja over alleged poor welfare.
NIG6407: Protesters marched in and around Agbor over a missing voter register for the area. The demonstration was peaceful.
NIG6404: No fewer than six persons sustained various degrees of injuries while about 15 houses were destroyed as youths attacked residents of Ogbetiti/Okeluche village in Ikenga Ogidi community, Idemili North Council Area. The attack is believed to have been motivated over the control of land.
NIG6408: Boko Haram attacks Bazza village. Date vague, causalities unknown.
NIG6405: Following an assault on Michika by Boko Haram, military forces launch a campaign to liberate the city, which included an air assault. During the battle, one known causality of note was the son of a former politician, all totalling 24. Boko Haram causalities not known - the fighting was reported as 'fierce.' As a result of the attack, the army has moved sensitive weapons from Mubi. Despite an early report the military had retaken the city, it was later learned Boko Haram maintained control of the area.
NIG6406: On 8 August 2014, military officials announced they had retaken Bama following a air bombing campaign. The dates of the bombing runs, causalities, and the actual transfer of territory were not reported. Despite the alleged takeover, later reports suggest that many of the villagers have died or are dying of starvation.
NIG6400: Unknown assailants attack several villages in Gusau LGA including Kofa, Kundubau, Wonaka, Fura Girke, Fegin Mahe, Gangara, Kukar Gandu, Kanawa, Lafiya, Gora, Akuzo, Zamfarawar Girke and Damba Model Primary School. Twenty deaths reported. Conflicting reports as to where the majority of causalities occurred.
NIG6403: Boko Haram attacks Michika, 'making strong gains' in several parts of the city. Boko Haram later claimed they had gained control over the entirety of the city. Causalities not known.
NIG6401: Twenty members of Boko Haram are killed (some sources claim 21) in an attempt to overtake Buratai and target a military commander. The attack took place during the morning hours. A school building was also razed.
NIG6402: 'Fierce' fighting between Boko Haram and military forces in Mubi. 'Scores' of [Boko Haram] killed in the fighting, soldiers reported injuries. Exact date is not known.
NIG6386: Boko Haram attacks and overtakes Duhu, Shuwa Kirshinga and 'other towns' on the night of 05/09 or the morning of 06/09. Causality numbers not provided.
NIG6391: At least six persons were allegedly killed and five others injured as a result of an attack on Lamba Gyambar community in Wase local government area of Plateau State. The unidentified assailants attacked the community around 11pm shooting sporadically and setting homes ablaze.
NIG6389: Military forces launched an attack on Boko Haram in Kawuri, killing 50 of its members. The attack was pre-emptive, as information was gathered that Boko Haram was planning an attack on nearby Konduga. Following the operation soldiers went on patrols in Konduga.
NIG6390: A group of members of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kwara State staged a protest against the state leadership of the party over alleged imposition of a candidate as the parties chairman in Ilorin West Local Government Area.
NIG6385: Boko Haram attacks and overtakes Gulak in the early hours of the day, causing residents to flee. Several residents from surrounding villages also fled. Causality not known.
NIG6384: Residents of Sabo-Oke area of Ilorin, Kwara State attacked workers of the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) who went there to disconnect electricity supply over unpaid debts. No reported injuries.
NIG6382: Residents of Otuoke protest, forcibly shutting down nearby Federal University. The protesters were angry that the management of the institution denied them employment and admission opportunities.
NIG6383: Members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ilorin-west Local Government Area of Kwara State protested the inauguration of a factional party chairman in the area.
NIG6380: Six are killed in a Fulani attack on a Eggon settlement. The attack occurred mid-morning. Some sources have the death total as high as 31.
NIG6378: The National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives (NANNM) staged a protest over alleged poor working conditions.
NIG6379: Students demonstrate along Benin-Ore federal highway outside Igouriakhi in protest over poor infrastructure and unpaid salaries of their lecturers.
NIG6381: Nigeria Union of Local Government Employees, NULGE, Kabba-Bunu branch protest non-payment of salaries.
NIG6373: During the early hours of the day unidentified gunmen burn a brewery and shoot sporadically. Witnesses place the death total between 50-55, others 18, though official reports hold the total at seven. Wukari is mainly Jukun, and it is believe the origin of the attack is related to the removal of the traditional ruler of the area.
NIG6374: 55 are reported killed following a Fulani attack on the Nasarawa-Eggon communities of Agbolagu, Kampani and Fadama-Bona.
NIG6377: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill the Chief Magistrate for Enugu South at his home, specific location unknown.
NIG6376: Boko Haram overtakes Bara without violence. Many residents flee into Cameroon.
NIG6375: Boko Haram overtakes Banki during the evening hours without violence. Many residents flee into Cameroon.
NIG6370: A group of Coca dealers protest at a local Ministry of Agriculture office over a levy directed at them.
NIG22882: On 1 September 2014, a group of 21 people in Lagos (Lagos Islands, Lagos) beat up a gay student after he was invited to the house of a man he had met at a party.
NIG6369: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attack and kill two police at Magama Gumau station in Toro LGA.
NIG6372: Boko Haram members reportedly took over Bama town - the second largest town in the state - and hoisted the sects flag, following a gun battle between they and Nigerian soldiers. 'Scores' killed before soldiers fled the city alongside civilians - thousands displaced. Military sources who spoke to journalists in Maiduguri said the soldiers were able to kill about 70 of the militants and injure about 30 others. Some reports have the death total as high as 130. The number of soldiers and civilians killed are not known. Despite several sources reporting the fall a Bama to Boko Haram, Xinhua and This Day (Lagos) reports the military repelled the attack, the latter describing the battle as Boko Harams 'Waterloo.' It is possible Boko Haram retreated, regrouped, and attacked again. A military airstrike was involved in the battle.
NIG6371: BringBackOurGirls supporters marked the 140 days of the abduction of Chibok schoolgirls in a protest condemning government inaction.
NIG6368: Suspected Boko Haram attack Jibwhiwhui village (and its immediate areas) over two days, killing 14.
NIG6366: Two persons were killed while many others were displaced in Shangev-Ya district of Kwande Local Government Area of Benue State, following a communal clash 'at the weekend' between Dzev and Mbakyaa communities.
NIG6367: Youths believed to be members of a faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Isoko South Local Government Area of Delta State forced the shutting down of the Erhioke Flow Station over the politics of the management company.
NIG6362: After gaining control of Gamboru from government forces on 25/08 residents report Boko Haram had been tracking residents who had fled the area and killing them. Residents said 42 people have been killed while many others have been abducted - many forcibly conscripted into the military. Dates of the specific killings not known.
NIG6365: Suspected Boko Haram attack Jibwhiwhui village (and its immediate areas) over two days, killing 14.
NIG6360: Unidentified gunmen attack an army post in a Bauchi suburb. The sources describes the attacks as 'insurgents,' but does not further attempt to identity the attackers. One soldier reported dead, another injured.
NIG6361: Boko Haram captures Dikwa and Marte town, raising their flag above the cities, with 'very little resistance from military forces.' The initial gunfire caused many of the residences to flee. Casualties not known. The attack occurred during the evening hours.
NIG6363: Suspected Boko Haram attack and overtake Dalwa. It appears this was done by the same group and the same operation as the excursion into Jibwhiwhui. Fourteen dead between the two towns.
NIG6358: Boko Haram reportedly takes over Wulgo. Date(s) unknown, violence unknown.
NIG6359: University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) workers protested against the storage in their morgue of the body of a doctor who died of the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) for fear of outbreak.
NIG6364: Scores of residents of Unity Estate, Igbogbo-Baiyeku Local Council Development Area, LCDA, protested to (or at, not known) the Lagos State House of Assembly over incessant violence against the community by some land grabbers popularly called 'Omo-Onile.'
NIG6352: Boko Haram attacks Miringa, destroys communication and snatched a sports utility vehicle belonging to the Borno State chairman of the All Progressives Congress.
NIG6349: Two House of Representatives aspirants and their allies or supporters clash in Ibadan, at least ten injuries.
NIG6350: Residents of the Downs-Quarters area of Kaduan protest the placing of a Ebola isolation centre in their area.
NIG6351: Supporters of the APC hold a protest in support of the removal of a council chairman.
NIG6356: A range of forty to sixty reported dead in a clash between Fulani/Alagoa (Fulani mercenaries) and Eggon militias in Tudun-Ababu, Wamba, Akwanga, Nasarawa Eggon - the source records the deaths exclusively at Tudun-Ababu. Victims of the troubled areas were seen moving their children and property to Lafia town. Clashes in the area between the two groups has been occurring since 23/08.
NIG6347: A group of doctors protest their dismissal by the federal government following a prolonged strike.
NIG6348: Commercial tricycle operators in Bayelsa State, popularly known as Keke Napep, protested against the alleged excessive use of force and extortion by policemen. The protest comes after police are believed to have mishandled a pregnant woman.
NIG6342: One person is killed and another injured by unidentified gunmen following an attack on Ungwan Mallam in Sanga LGA.
NIG6338: Six are killed in Kafin Hausa by unidentified attackers.
NIG6343: Two villages in Wukari LGA are attacked by suspected Fulani gunmen. The attack caused villagers to flee and the destruction for their crops, causalities not known. The twin attacks comes only a day after two other villages in the area were attacked.
NIG6345: Boko Haram attack and overtake Gamboru and Ngala towns, along the border with Cameroon. The also caused all military forces in nearby Ngala to flee as well, allowing Boko Haram to enter that town without resistance. In a response to the attacks, the Nigerian Air Force jet later dropped a massive bomb in the middle of Gamboru after hovering for several minutes in the air. The jet then left while the militants began a house-to-house raid in Gamboru. The attack occurred early in the morning. The attackers later attempted to destroy a bridge linking Nigeria with Cameroon.
NIG6341: A group of lawyers protest the continued failure of a government server to function property, causing a backlog of work.
NIG6340: Fulani and Eggos militias clash in various unarticulated locations over several days in Lafia and Obi LGAs. Though the battles began at the beginning of the week details of the clashes become more detailed on 26/09 and 27/08. Causality details unknown.
NIG6334: Gunmen attack Nwuban (Wumban), Muba (Jikun) and Nbishi villages of Wukari LGA. 13 reported killed 50 houses destroyed. Some sources claim 20 dead plus 85 injured. The identities of the attackers are believed to be Fulani.
NIG6336: Boko Haram takes over Madagali town of Adamawa State, including a Catholic Church building. 'Dozens' killed. Exact date not known.
NIG6331: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill a police officer after trailing him to his home from a mosque.
NIG6337: Boko Haram attacks and overtakes Banki. Many military members managed to escape and fled towards Amhide villages before they entered Cameroon for safety. Causalities not known, however, sources said many casualties were recorded including Boko Haram, security operatives and civilians who were caught up in the crossfire.
NIG6333: Fulani and Eggos militias clash in various unarticulated locations over several days in Lafia and Obi LGAs. Though the battles began at the beginning of the week details of the clashes become more detailed on 26/09 and 27/08. Causality details unknown.
NIG6328: Property destruction: Unidentified attackers burn down a church in Sabon Garin Hyanbula - a location in Jigawa State. No causalities or injuries reported.
NIG6329: Youths in Emohua community of Rivers State have protest against the setting up of an Ebola quarantine centre in their area by the state government for fear of outbreak.
NIG6330: No fewer than 17 people were reported killed and scores injured in a renewed clash between Fulani herdsmen and Eggon farmers at Fadaman Bauna, Achigogo in Lafia LGA. The attack occurred during the evening hours when Eggon youths attacked the Fulani village. The attack is believed to be motivated revenge for past Fulani attacks.
NIG6335: A group of traders protest the destruction of their structures by the government.
NIG6327: Unidentified gunmen, likely Fulani, attack Bishu village of Wukari killing six.
NIG6324: Okada riders, believed to be mostly Chadian, clash with police during a protest. The reason for the protest is not known. Much of the property in the area was reported destroyed.
NIG6325: Fulani and Eggos militias clash in various unarticulated locations over several days in Lafia and Obi LGAs. Though the battles began at the beginning of the week details of the clashes become more detailed on 26/09 and 27/08. Causality details unknown.
NIG6323: Unidentified gunmen attack and kill three at a police checkpoint at Tillei location. The attack occurred during the night-time hours.
NIG6322: CISLAC gathers to protest a tax.
NIG6317: Boko Haram insurgents have taken over the Police Mobile Training camp - a police academy - in Limankara village. It was gathered that there was heavy fighting between the insurgents and troops before the camp finally fell. It is believed Boko Haram targeted the facility after reported attempts from security forces to dislodge Boko Harams control from Gwoza, which had fallen under BH control several weeks earlier. Numerous trainees ('scores') were killed or seriously injured by the attackers, no numbers provided. It was later determined by Vanguard that 35 officers were declared missing following the attack. Following the takeover a video was released by the group declaring a caliphate in the area.
NIG6318: Hundreds of traders in Abuja staged a peaceful protest against imposition of multiple taxes on them by Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC).
NIG6319: Inhabitants of Igbei community in Auchi, Etsako West Local Government Area of Edo State on Thursday (21/08) took to the streets to protest alleged state government take over of their land, despite a court order.
NIG6320: Youths in Patani Local Council took to the streets protesting the alleged imposition of a council chairmanship candidate who opposed President Johanthan, who they support.
NIG6321: Residents protest the poor state of local roads in Abule Ado.
NIG6315: Boko Haram attack and overtake Buni Yadi, raising their flag over the town. Of any deaths three are known - two villagers were executed for smoking cigarettes, a third for dealing drugs. Many other residents have fled to neighbouring towns. Date(s) of the attack not entirely known.
NIG6316: Two factions of MASSOB clash at a headquarters in Okwe over internal political strife. Four believed dead.
NIG6313: A gathering of APC and PDP supporters degenerates into violence when a controversial PDP lawmaker arrives to move forward with a gubernatorial impeachment vote. Four killed, one critically injured.
NIG6306: A group of 100+ youth protest the killing of a man by the anti-robbery police division.
NIG6307: The BringBackOurGirls Group protests at Asokoro junction for the release of the abducted Chibok girls.
NIG6305: Members of an Anglican Church protest the destruction of their sanctuary by 'thugs', which occurred late last week. The protest occurred in various locations in Onitsha, though the church building itself is in nearby Oyi LGA.
NIG6308: Members of the Lagos State chapter, Nigeria Medical Association (NMA) at the Teaching Hospital, Idi-Araba staged a protest over the sacking of 16,000 resident doctors in the country by the federal government.
NIG6309: Hundreds of doctors took to major streets in Lagos, Ibadan, Akure in Ondo State, to protest against the purported sacking of 16,000 resident doctors.
NIG6311: Meat sellers protest low patronage due to the outbreak of Ebola disease. The women under the aegis of Bushmeat Sellers Association lamented that since the announcement that the deadly disease could be caused by eating bush meat, spell had been cast on their sales. The protest took place at the governors office.
NIG6298: Two persons have been reportedly killed in the early hours of the day by unknown attackers at Rafin Bwaunan Noma community in Bassa Local government Area of Plateau State. The victims included a 41 year old man and a young girl.
NIG6300: Boko Haram attacks Ala in a suspected coordinated attack that extends 'between Dikwa and Marte towns.' Causalities reported, but are not town specific and are not enumerated. Date is vague.
NIG6301: Boko Haram attacks Alabanya and Kaje in a series of coordinated attacks throughout the region. Fatalities are reported, numbers not known (coded as 10). Exact date is not known, ~17/08.
NIG6302: Riding motorcycles, members of Boko Haram attack Dikwa. 'They killed many people (numbers not known) and destroyed many houses.' The attack is believed to be in revenge for the town rising up against Boko Haram by mobilising vigilante militias. Date of the attack is vague.
NIG6303: Boko Haram attacks Mafa, date not known, ~17/08. The attack may have been in conjunction with an attack on Dikwa.
NIG6304: A security official reports seeing corpses (numbers not known, coded as 10) in Marte on 17/08. It is not clear when the date of the attack was. Boko Haram is blamed for the attack.
NIG6299: Suspected insurgents (not named) ambushed and burnt down a police patrol vehicle at Tumu village in Akko Local Government Area of Gombe State. Injuries reported, no causalities.
NIG6293: Unknown gunmen have invaded Bara on motorcycles killing two persons, destroying Local Government Secretariat, Local Government Lodge, EPI Office, Court and Local Government Staff Quarters.
NIG6295: Suspected PDP militia attack four Rivers State communities, Okomoko, Egwi and Ulakwo 1 & 2 in an effort believed to be motivated by the desire for the political supremacy of Etche LGA. An Air Force officer and solider were believed to have been killed in the attacks and fighting. Exact date(s) unknown. Attacks occurred 'at the weekend.'
NIG6292: Students of Osun State University riot violently after it is learned that several of their fellow students may be punished following a recent accident.
NIG6294: A clash between supporters of the state governor, Rochas Anayo Okorocha, and that of the deputy speaker, House of Representatives. Hon. Emeka Ihedioha is reported of a local festival in Ahiazu Mbaise LGA - no exact location provided. The clash is attributed to the contest for power between the two politicians ahead of the 2015 general elections. No injuries reported. The clash took place 'at the weekend.'
NIG6291: Protesting students clash with police, leaving four people hospitalized. The protest which was staged by the students of the Olabisi Onabanjo University, Ago-Iwoye, was for further reduction of school fees after government had reduced the fees. The students had earlier in the week stormed the entrance of the Governor's Office, Oke-Mosan, protesting the reduction of school fees in all the state-owned institutions. The situation turned chaotic on 15/08 when the students attempted to block the Ibara Government Reservation road, in order to ground vehicular movement.
NIG6289: A group men protested against the killing of two persons by a policeman attached to the Iba Police Post at Iyana School Bus Stop. The protesters, who chanted war songs and held dangerous weapons, remained on the streets for more than three hours, threatening to set the police station on fire. The police maintain they were attacked by criminals, causing the killing.
NIG6290: PHCN members protest at Sapele power station over unpaid back wages.
NIG6288: Youths in Southern Kaduna (Unguwan Wakili) have protest against the endorsement of President Goodluck Jonathan for the 2015 Presidency by Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and top government functionaries from their area. It is not clear if the youths identified with the PDP themselves. There was a police presence at the protest site, which restricted the group from entering a PDP convention hall.
NIG6287: Protest for and against the announcement for fees reduction by the Ogun State government turned bloody as students of the Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU), Ago-Iwoye and those of Moshood Abiola Polytechnic (MAPOLY), engaged in a free for all fight. The students from the polytechnic had staged a rally in support of the fee reduction by the government while the university students staged a protest against the move.
NIG6286: Members of the APC blame the PDP for an attack against the home of the Minister of State for Education, which left seven people injured. The attack is believed to be in relation to several other disturbances between the PDP and APC around the Port Harcourt metro on 13/08.
NIG6283: Business and commercial activities were disrupted in parts of Port Harcourt, the Rivers State capital following clashes between supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), ahead of the planned visit of Governor Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi to Rumueprikom community in Obio/Akpor local government area of the state. The clashes were said to have started at the popular Wimpey Junction along Ikwerre Road in Port Harcourt, and later spread to Rumueme, also in Obio/Akpor local government area, and Diobu, in Port Harcourt City local government area. Several injuries reported.
NIG6279: Protesters of the NLC protest at the headquarters of a bank over its debt.

NIG6241: Parents of secondary students enrolled in a public school in Osogbo protest at the office of the headmaster for improved boarding facilities. The group gave a five-day ultimatum before embarking on a mass protest.

NIG6195: A peaceful demonstration was embarked upon by workers of Jos-North Local Council Area of Plateau State to protest against the non-payment of allowances. The protests lasted two consecutive days. NULGE was a key organizer of the protests.

NIG6129: Students of Ogun State origin from the Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta (FUNAAB) staged a protest in Abeokuta over non-payment of their 2013/2014 bursary.
NIG6131: One person feared dead as members of Peoples Democratic Party attacked members of the All Progressive Congress at Ile-Ife. NIG6133: A vigilante militia unsuccessfully attempted to lynch a suspected kidnapper.
NIG6132: The anti-vandal Team of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) have been attacked by Nigeria Police officers in the early hours of the day in Niger State, northcentral Nigeria. NIG6127: Unidentified gunmen in the night-time opened fire on a group of Muslim worshippers in Bukuru, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, injuring three persons. The attack occurred at 9pm.
NIG6123: Suspected Boko Haram disguised in army uniforms killed seven people in an attack near the northeastern border with Cameroon. The gunmen, five of whom were also killed, razed a police station, a military camp and other buildings.
NIG6124: A suspected member of Boko Haram (later identified as a 'kingpin' is killed in a shootout with security operatives in the Kinkino area of Kaduna South. The gun exchange was said to have lasted for a few hours, causing panic among the residents of the area.

NIG6126: BringBackOurGirls protesters attempt to baricade the Presidential Villa in the Aso Rock area, but are blocked by security forces.

NIG6116: No fewer than 50 [Boko Haram], five soldiers and one senior officer died on Friday night when some militants attacked the troops bases and police locations in Damboa. NIG6110: Okada riders protest the killing of a colleague by a hit-and-run driver.
