Boko Haram has yet to claim responsibility, though authorities believe they are responsible. After 24 hours four more victims succumbed to their injuries. One report from United News of Bangladesh Limited has the death toll at 30.
NIG4170: Unidentified gunmen abducted the former Vice Chancellor of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Prof. Ilochi Okafor. The kidnapping may be political, as Prof. Okafor is a possible gubernatorial candidate in the next election cycle.
NIG4166: Gunmen attacked the First Baptist Church in Sango Ota, Ogun State, killing two worshippers and injuring four others. The attackers took valuables from the victims before opening fire on them.
NIG4167: At least two people were feared killed while undetonated explosives were also discovered in a residence of a retired police officer in Gudum Sayawa, a suburb of Bauchi metropolis.
NIG4163: Twenty females who wearing were wearing 'mini skirts' were killed by unidentified, yet suspected to be Boko Haram militants in various locations throughout the city. The effected neighbourhoods of the city included Gwange, London Chiki, Abbagaram and Kaleri. The following that JTF authorities denied any such attacks took place.
NIG4162: A JTF team uncovers a bomb making factory in Mubi and makes one arrest of a Boko Haram leader.
NIG4164: Weapons Seizure: Chief of Army Staff Lieutenant General Azubuike Ihejirika publicly stated soldiers have seized weapons, huge sums of money and vehicles meant for suicide bombings over a period of time 'in the north-east.' Exact date(s) unknown. The announcement was made in Abuja.
NIG4160: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen kill two persons in Shokwari Ward on the evening of 22 November.
NIG4157: Four are killed in a riot of Islamic youths who had heard rumors of blasphemy against the prophet Muhammad from a local. A church and other shops were burned. This was revealed by eyewitnesses who told reporters in Kano, that the violence erupted as a result of a communication breakdown between a non-Muslim tailor and a Muslim man over an inscription on a dress designed by the tailor. Ten involved were later arrested.
NIG4159: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen kill three persons in Polo Ward on the evening of 22 November.
NIG4156: A group of 300 protest proposed maritime boundary demarcation among Cameroon and Nigeria in a border town.
NIG4155: Five persons were reported killed and 15 houses set ablaze in the Obi Local Government Area of Nasarawa State in renewed clashes between Koro and Eggon tribesmen. The clash took place in the Gwadanye area of Agyaragu.
NIG4153: A labor protest descends into riot when workers demanding payment storm the Plateau State House assembly, causing those inside to flee.
NIG4154: A Fulani herdsman rapes a newly wed Ketu (Yoruba) female.
NIG4150: 100 workers of Omala Local Government Area of Kogi State protested over unpaid salaries. According to an eyewitness, the workers stormed the council headquarters in Abejukolo at about 8. 00am, singing war songs and demanding the removal of a local council chairman.
NIG4149: A protesting labor union demonstrates outside the State House in Jos to demand back payment for seven months of salary.
NIG4148: Students of University of Abuja on Monday protested the failure of the university management to meet up with the six months period given it to accredit some of its courses.
NIG4147: Members of the PDP and AC clash after AC attacks a PDP election office, burning it to the ground. Five reported injured.
NIG4152: A group of Christian women protest against the operation of nude hotels, sex hawking, and indecent dressing among others.
NIG4151: A group of unnamed gunmen attacked a group of migrating Fulanis, killing 12, as well as 12 of their cattle. (The perpetrators are described as 'A group of notorious gunmen,' but no names are provided.)
NIG4142: Following the killing of a Muslim by a Christian vigilante group, riots erupt, causing four initial deaths and property damage. The death toll later rose to 10. Police make over 50 arrests in following days.
NIG4143: On 18 November 2012, a Christian armed group killed a Muslim resident in Ibi (Ibi, Taraba) who insisted on going through their illegal checkpoint, triggering riots.
NIG4144: The former Chairman of Ikeja Local Government, Lagos State, and ex Special Adviser to Governor Babatunde Fashola on Health during his first term in office, Oluwatoyin Hamzat, was assassinated by unknown gunmen in the Sabo area of Shagama.
NIG4146: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen shot and killed a Christian cleric in his home.
NIG4145: Unidentified gunmen on motorcycles shoot and kill a police officer and a bystander civilians for unknown reasons. It is believed the group of gunmen are the same group that attack a Zaria hotel the previous evening.
NIG4140: Unidentified gunmen launch an attack on a Zaria hotel.
NIG4141: Unidentified gunmen Saturday night killed a lawmaker, Ibrahim Abba Garko, of the ANPP, in the Unguwa Uku area of the city.
NIG4138: Thousands of flood-displaced persons in relief camps in the Bayelsa capital, Yenagoa, on Thursday protested their eviction from the camps by the State Government.
NIG4135: Seven are injured in a clash between supporters of AC and those of PDP. The clash began after a disagreement over the placement of their candidates political posters around the city.
NIG4137: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen kill three traders in Maiduguri. The gunmen, according to an eyewitness and resident of Bulabulin ward, Chindo Ibrahim, stormed the traders' shops in a tricycle, chanting God is great and started firing gunshots into the air to scare people away from the area.
NIG4139: Unidentified gunmen kill six members of the same family in the early morning hours.
NIG4134: Military forces claim to have killed a high profile Boko Haram commander responsible for the assassination of a retired general on 2 November.
NIG4136: Unidentified gunmen launch an attack on JTF personnel. In retaliatory fire four of the gunmen were injured and subsequently arrested.
NIG4132: Unidentified 'thugs' attack a group of protesting students, who were gathered to call for a government payment of tuition.
NIG4131: Unidentified gunmen killed the Director of Design and Construction in the Borno State Ministry of Water Resources, Mallam Ali Mohammed Sheriff in Maiduguri. This action appears to be an assassination.
NIG4133: A suspected Boko Haram member detonates a suicide car bomb near a church, claims eight lives plus injuries.
NIG4129: Gunmen suspected to be of Boko Haram sect attacked Ummarari and Galadima wards of the metropolis, killing a University of Maiduguri (UNIMAID) don, Alhaji Babagana Kola and a director in the Ministry of Land and Survey Mallam Yerima.
NIG4130: Soldiers open fire on a group of rioters in Delta State. The rioters were attempting vigilante justice against a local whom they believed was a member of Boko Haram. 6 of the rioting group dead, many more injured. In a reprisal attack, irate villagers razed the palace of Ovie of Idjerhe, His Royal Majesty, Erhikevwe I, who, they suspected, invited the soldiers.
NIG4127: No fewer than 15 persons were feared injured when supporters of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) on Monday, clashed in Gboko and Makurdi areas of Benue State. ACN members were holding a meeting at a hotel in Gboko when persons suspected to be PDP members, stormed the venue thus triggering the fight.
NIG4128: Unknown gunmen kidnap a journalists wife and two children at their home. It is unclear if the attack was motivated by ransom or politics.
NIG4126: Suspected Boko Haram bomb a cattle market in the Gwange area, kill one.
NIG4124: Gunmen have shot dead five Christian residents of a town in a restive northeastern Nigerian region previously hit by deadly Islamist attacks, however, the perpetrator is not known here, nor is it evident that victims were killed because they were Christians.
NIG4125: Suspect Boko Haram gunmen raid a police station, kill one officer and wound another.
NIG4121: Members of the Onitsha Market Traders' Association gathered at the Anambra State Government House in Awka to protest continuous molestation of them by the state's revenue agents.
NIG4122: Following a police station attack, suspected Boko Haram attack and burn three churches, though they did not cause any causality.
NIG4123: Unidentified attackers throw a hand grenade into a cattle market in the mid-morning hours in Gambouru area.
NIG4120: Boko Haram attacks and kills three police officers outside a police station in Yobe, break into the complex and steal weapons soon after.
NIG4118: Labours protest the closure of a factory and the non-payment of salaries over the past six months.
NIG4114: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill a village head and his family. It is unclear if this is ethnic or political violence.
NIG4116: Gunmen shot and killed two Chinese construction workers in rural Borno state, motive unknown.
NIG4115: Unidentified gunmen attack a group of riot police for unknown reasons.
NIG4117: An IED targeted at a group of JTF soldiers explodes, but causes no bodily harm. Following the explosion several gunshots were heard by witnesses.
NIG4113: Hundreds of ex-militants barricaded the only road into Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, over the non-payment of their allowances over a period of six months.
NIG4110: Unknown insurgents invade a village, kill a family of four for unknown reasons.
NIG4111: Unknown armed men attack and kill three Fulani ethnic herders in an apparent act of revenge. The event occurred in a location known as Fadan Karshi.
NIG4109: A clash between police and okada riders causes nine injures.
NIG4106: Twin Boko Haram bomb blasts, targeting soldiers, kill two civilians.
NIG4107: Motorcycle couriers protest the police following the shooting of a colleague. Police respond with teargas.
NIG4108: Okada Riders attack a police station, torching five vehicles and seven motorcycles. It is not clear if the police responded.
NIG4112: The JTF raid a Boko Haram hideout, four insurgents are killed in a short clash.
NIG4103: A group of retired police officers gather to protest the non-payment of their pensions.
NIG4105: Unknown gunmen attack and kill two soldiers along Potiskum-Maiduguri road.
NIG4102: Motorcycle couriers clash with highway police, one dead.
NIG4104: Over 500 separatists who took part in the declaration of the Republic of Biafra on Monday have been arrested by the police. It is unclear if violence occurred between the actors.
NIG4100: Suspected Boko Haram kill three outside a house. 'The three gunmen came on a motorcycle and opened fire on their victims who had just parked outside a house,' Kano state police spokesman Mustapha Abubakar told AFP.
NIG4099: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attacked a police station, set fire to a primary school and destroyed several cell phone towers in the early morning hours. Witnesses saw the bodies of two police officers being carried out of the police station, though this was not substantiated.
NIG4101: Arrests: Police arrest 25 gunmen suspected of the killing of a police officer the previous day. It is unclear if any of the suspects had affiliations with Boko Haram.
NIG4098: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill a police officer in an attack. A suspect was later arrested.
NIG4097: Victims displaced by a recent flood gathered to protest the governments poor handling of funds and materials donated to them.
NIG4095: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen set fire to several government buildings and over 20 houses, three reported killed.
NIG4096: A retired Nigerian general, Mohammed Shuwa, is shot and killed, along with a guest at his home. The motive seems to be assassination. Boko Haram is suspected, but denies involvement.
NIG4091: Soldiers systematically shot and killed more than 40 civilians in the Kalari neighborhood, believing they had connections to Boko Haram. Dozens of men were forced from their homes in house to house searches in Maiduguri and marched to an open field where their faces were compared to photographic databases. Some were separated and then shot. Reports said 48 died, others 39, still others 70. In October, soldiers shot dead more than 30 civilians and burned homes in Maiduguri after a bomb suspected to have been planted by the sect killed a lieutenant. Following the attacks soldiers occupied the Kalari area of the city.
NIG4094: Unidentified gunmen kill four civilians and a security officer before they escaped. These gunmen are believed to be the same as those who attacked Jwol location.
NIG4093: Unidentified gunmen opened fire on a group of police on patrol, killing a corporal.
NIG4090: Boko Harem gunmen shoot and kill the chairman of and ANPP and a prominent businessman near their residential neighbourhood.
NIG4089: Two policemen were killed by gunmen suspected to be 'cultists.'
NIG4086: Protesting applicants in their hundreds stormed the Ministry of Interior in Abuja over what they described as the rejection of their applications for various paramilitary jobs. Security officials fired their side arms into the air to disperse the crowd.
NIG4088: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, invade a small town, torch a police station and a Christian/religious primary school. The attack began in the early evening, so it is not clear if civilians were present in the school. Causalities not reported.
NIG4087: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, invade a small town, torch a police station and a primary school. Causalities not reported.
NIG4085: Leaders communities in Akuku-Toru Local Government Area of Rivers State on protested against the alleged plan to cede oil wells in the council to neighboring Bayelsa State.
NIG4082: Fulani militiamen attack a pub, kill four of the patrons and injuring seven others. It is not clear if this is a ethno-religious attack.
NIG4083: Following the attack on a Catholic church a group of Christian youths angrily assaulted several Muslims passing by the Church in an act of revenge. One individual is burned alive by the mob. Also, Muslim youths in their strongholds, of Tudun Wada, Rigassa and Kawo were said to have armed themselves in readiness for any possible reprisals from Christians.
NIG4084: A suicide bomber rammed an SUV loaded with explosives into a Catholic church holding Mass on Sunday in northern Nigeria, killing at eight fifteen people and wounding 145 others. Some witnesses said the death toll could be as high as 12. They said the dead included children. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack. Christian youths retaliated against a group of Muslims following the blast, believing Boko Haram, or another Islamic group responsible. The death toll grew as the day wore on.
NIG4081: A explosion, believed to be a bomb, injures two in rural Bauchi State.
NIG4080: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, kill the son of a political figure.
NIG4079: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attack the home of a man and set him ablaze.
NIG4078: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, have burnt the house of a village head in Gwaje, Alhaji Mohammed Salisu Auwal, and killed two of his children. Witness: 'The gunmen ransacked my neighbours house, tied down the two kids, believed to be the biological sons of the village head inside the house and burnt them beyond recognition.'
NIG4076: The headmaster of Ari Primary School, Musa Magazai and one Mallam Galtamari, along with his two children, were killed in the early hours by gunmen suspected to be members of the Boko Haram sect. The killings were perpetrated despite the 4pm-7am curfew imposed by Governor Ibrahim Gaidam last Monday.
NIG4072: An IED explodes in a crowed market, causalities unknown.
NIG4074: Commercial cyclists popularly known as okada on Monday marched through some major streets in Lagos, protesting the state government's fresh clampdown and seizure of their bikes. Many attacked police officers and vandalized property.
NIG4070: An explosive device targeting a military patrol went off on a road in Nigeria's northeastern city of Potiskum, setting the vehicle on fire. There were at least six soldiers on board the car, but their status is unclear. A nearby market was affected by the blast as well.
NIG4071: Defusal: Police forces discover and successfully control-detonate an explosive hidden within the grounds of Gombe State University.
NIG4066: Residents discover the bodies of nine people they charge were killed by soldiers hunting suspects in a roadside bomb blast four days earlier.
NIG4067: Eight people are killed after a Boko Haram attack, the third in as many days for the city. At least 30 dead over the course of the campaign, though the JTF say this number is inaccurate, asserting the number is closer to 13. The local hospital counts 23.
NIG4068: Arrests: JTF forces arrest a senior commander of Boko Haram, but decline to share his name. The arrest occurred at the home of the former governor of Borno State.
NIG4069: On 20 October 2012, some electorates protested at the INEC polling station in Akure (Akure South, Ondo) over poor distribution of ballot materials to polling stations in the area.
NIG4064: A Chinese construction worker and three Nigerian civilians are shot and killed by suspected Boko Haram.
NIG4065: Suspected Boko Haram detonates an IED outside a church at 11am. Four killed in the attack, three injured. Hundreds of residents flee the city following the three days of attacks.
NIG4063: Security forces discover and dispose of unexploded bombs throughout the city. Authorities believe the explosives were planted by Boko Haram.
NIG4060: Multiple explosions occur throughout the city for the second straight day, detonated by suspected Boko Haram. A military source said some buildings had been destroyed by homemade bombs and a security checkpoint was attacked, death toll stands at 11.
NIG4059: Suspected Boko Haram attack a suspected security checkpoint. Two soldiers sustain injuries.
NIG4062: The bloody clash between Fulani herdsmen and Eggon farmers in Kadarko Community in Nasarawa State, has left three people dead.
NIG4058: Fulani herdsmen have attacked a bus killing four people in Gwatukuru village near Dass Local Government Area in Bauchi State. Nine injured.
NIG4055: A bomb detonates in a industrial area, no injury reported.
NIG4053: Following a Boko Haram bomb attack against them, soldiers retaliated against civilians. Four houses burnt and witnesses heard gunshots.
NIG4056: An explosion damages a church building, no reported causalities.
NIG4052: A bomb targeting soldiers is detonated by Boko Haram. 24 killed in the explosion, soldiers retaliated against local civilians following the attack.
NIG4057: Multiple explosions targeting JTF forces in a market cause injury, but no death. Perpetrators unknown.
NIG4054: About 2,000 block traffic in protest of a stone quarry company, which they believe have not paid agreed upon royalties to the town.
NIG4051: Students at the Osun State College of Education riot in protest of two colleagues killed in a car accident. Fifteen injured, vehicles vandalized.
NIG4050: Two of a fire fight that killed 24 suspected members of Boko Haram. Zannari areas of Lagos street
NIG4044: During a fire fight between Boko Haram and JTF forces 10 civilians are allegedly killed by Boko Haram in crossfire. Following the battle military command disputed this claim. Zannari areas of Lagos street
NIG4049: The police detonate an IED after it was discovered by a local opposite a motor park. There were no causalities reported.
NIG4042: Members of the JTF shoot and kill 24 suspected members of Boko Haram while repelling an attack. The militants launched their attacks from the homes of civilians late Monday night and a protracted fire fight carried into the following morning. Conflicting report: the Daily Trust claims the death count was 54. Zannari areas of Lagos street
NIG4043: Classmates of a murdered student protest against the violence, throw stones at police when they attempt to disperse the crowd.
NIG4045: At least 15 separate explosions in targeting JTF forces punctuated by gunfire echoed Monday across a Maiduguri city, leaving more than 10 persons dead and telecommunication masts burnt. The explosions started at about 5.15pm and was on intermittently for about 30 minutes and sending serious panic among the people, according to a witness. The violence affected three broad areas. Gunmen killed a 'traffic warden' in this location.
NIG4048: Witnesses said a gunman suspected to belong to Boko Haram shot dead a police traffic warden in the city within view of a military checkpoint. The gunman simply walked away after the attack unstopped, witnesses said.
NIG4039: Four members of a family are killed as they exited a church. Boko Haram is suspected, though authorities cannot determine why this specific group was targeted.
NIG4040: Unknown assailants, disguised as police, attack a mosque in rural Kaduna, as well as the home of a local leader, killing at least 24 people in the pre dawn hours. Some believe the perpetrators were a local band of thieves seeking revenge, others, Boko Haram.
NIG4041: Nomadic Muslim herdsmen attacked a rural Christian village in central Nigeria over long-running land disputes, killing at least 30 people. The name of the village attacked is unknown or not provided.
NIG4038: A blast, seemingly targeting soldiers, detonates, but causes no causalities. Authorities believe the perpetrators are of Boko Haram.
NIG4037: Unidentified gunmen kidnap the Rivers State Commissioner for Power, Mr. Augustine Nwokocha, along with his assistant. The perpetrators may have been pirates seeking ransom, witch is common in the area, though the facts are unclear.
NIG4036: Youths take to the streets to protest the killing of a man they believe was beaten by the police.
NIG4033: Members of the PDP hold a political rally in protest of internal factions of the party which they believe are working counter to the vision of the party.
NIG4034: Four are killed in three separate towns (names unknown or not provided) in a Riyom district over a continuing conflict. The death tool raised to 20 over the course of a week.
NIG4035: Around 12 October 2012 (as reported), some workers of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) protested in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, imo) over the failure of the Commission to pay their wages.
NIG4030: A 75 year-old woman, along with her three children are killed by unknown gunmen. Fulani herdsman were later suspected, and several were arrested in connection with the murders.
NIG4031: Hausa Muslims and Berom youths clashed over a disputed land where Muslims usually used for their praying ground during Islamic festivals. One person is allegedly killed.
NIG4032: Hundreds of residents of housing estate gather outside the National Assembly building to protest its planned demolition by the government.
NIG4029: A day following similar violence, a Fulani militia attacked Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau, 14 reported deaths. The attack may have been directed at Berom ethnic Christians, however this information is not clear. Conflicting information asserts 21 deaths over two days of attacks.
NIG4027: Unknown gunmen yesterday bombed a police station and Unity Bank branch in Gwaram town in Jigawa State with Improvised Explosive Devices (IED). Though the perpetrators were unidentified, Boko Haram has engaged in similar activities in the past.
NIG4028: Unidentified gunmen on motor bikes attacked a Federal Road Safety Commission (FRSC) patrol vehicle, killing two officers and injuring one seriously. The motivation for the violence was not speculated on.
NIG4025: Cross River lawmakers left the state house and went into the streets to protest the Federal Governments decision not to appeal the judgment of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) which ceded the oil-rich Bakassi Peninsula to the Republic of Cameroon. The protest march ended at the governors office with Governor Liyel Imoke appealing for calm.
NIG4026: Students gather to protest a rate and fee hike of the university. Police react to the demonstration with an increased presence, but to not engage the students.
NIG4021: Two unidentified men assassinate a Enugu State monarch, or traditional ruler, at this shop. Police make several arrests in connection to the murder later in the week.
NIG4022: Three Christian Berom farmers are killed by Islamic Fulanis, adding to the ongoing ethnic strife.
NIG4023: Two policemen escorting immunization officials were shot dead today by gunmen on motorcycles at Kofar Dawanau area of Kano metropolis. It was later learned Boko Haram was responsible, and arrests were made.
NIG4018: Residents of Ajeromi Ifelodun Local Council of Lagos State march to the headquarters of an electric company to protest a recent rate hike due to a recently imposed tax.
NIG4019: Students of the University of Port Harcourt burn houses and cars in protest the recent killing riot and killing of four of their colleagues.
NIG4020: Students block the entrance to state offices, preventing the governor and his deputy from entering. The group was protesting an alleged non-payment of their bursary allowances.
NIG4012: Nigerian soldiers angry about the killing of two soldiers in a Boko Haram blast, shot dead more than 30 civilians and seven soldiers in thoughtless rage. A witness saw that soldiers had set fire to about 50 homes and businesses around the area, which sits near the Nigerian Union of Journalists state office and other buildings in Maiduguri. It appeared the soldiers attacked the area using assault rifles and heavy machine guns mounted on armored personnel carriers. Rounds shot from the heavy machine guns destroyed cars and set roofs on fire, which razed buildings and caused damage at a two-story shopping complex. The military later denied the ever occurred.
NIG4015: Unidentified people attack a political headquarters of the PDP as factious members protest party policy.
NIG4011: Suspected Boko Haram (though they did not claim responsibility) detonate a remote controlled explosive near the local headquarters of the Nigeria Union of Journalists. Two passerby soldiers were wounded in the attack when their van drive over the device. Conflicting account: several local residents claim to see six dead taken away by medical units.
NIG4017: Unidentified gunmen attack the official residence of an army commandant, killing at least one member of security personnel.
NIG4013: A motorcycle delivery/taxi group protest the newly imposed restriction to certain roads.
NIG4009: Mala Kaka, a traditional ruler outspoken against Boko Haram is shot and killed in his home.
NIG4010: Unidentified gunmen kidnap the majority leader of the Benus State House assembly, Paul Biam (PDP), and release him 24 hours later. It is unclear if the motive for kidnap was political or criminal.
NIG4008: JTF members raid a Boko Haram hideout, kill 30, including a senior leader, second-in-command Bakaka, and arrest 11. Conflicting report: some sources claim 31 deaths and 10 arrests.
NIG4003: Unknown gunmen have attacked Dogon Kuka village in Yobe State, killing 17. At least two victims died immediately. Authorities will not specify if they believe Boko Haram is a suspect.
NIG4004: Boko Haram gunmen attack a small town market with firearms, killing three Chinese construction workers an a Nigeria aid.
NIG4006: Boko Haram gunmen clash with JTF members in two separate areas of Damaturu. No deaths reports, several gunmen arrested.
NIG4007: Kwarbai Community Forum in Zaria Local Government Area of Kaduna State at the weekend protested over the arrest of its member and his family for allegedly involvement in Boko Harams activities.
NIG4000: A violent mob killed four university students who they believed were thieves. The victims were stripped naked, beaten with sticks, doused with petrol and set ablaze with tires around their necks.
NIG4001: A explosion near a television station kills a woman and wounded five children. It is unclear who the perpetrators were.
NIG4002: A teachers union protested the cancellation of World Teachers Day by gathering the singing anti-government songs.
NIG3999: Suspected Boko Haram detonate an explosive at a beer garden. Three reported deaths, 12 injuries. Conflicting reports (Xinhua) have one killed, 11 injured.
NIG3992: Unidentified people attack a Labour Party campaign rally. LP leader publicly blame a rival, Action Congress, though this could be a political maneuver. Later in the week it was learned the attackers were cultists.
NIG3994: An explosion detonated by unknown persons causes seven causalities, which of whom were brought to a military hospital. Conflicting report: The depots Public Relations Officer, Capt. Ibrahim Abdullahi, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Zaria that no death was recorded in the incident.
NIG3995: One person is dead and 10 others injured when a explosive detonates in a hotel/ Boko Haram is suspected.
NIG3998: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill two University of Maiduguri students. Authorities are uncertain if it was the work of Boko Haram.
NIG3996: Rival political groups clash following protests. It was reported that the AC was present, but its rival remained unnamed, though it is likely the PDP: Peoples Democratic Party. No injuries reported, though fighting lasted over half and hour.
NIG3989: JTF forces shoot and kill two suspects in connection to a shooting in a government housing complex which killed twenty.
NIG3981: Gunmen, suspected to Boko Haram, opened fire in a student housing area near a polytechnic school in the northeastern Nigerian city of Mubi, killing at least 40 and injuring at least 15 others. In the following days the death count was raised to 48 and a curfew was imposed. It was later learned the gunmen personally knew their victims, specifically targeting Christians. The following week it was determined by authorities the perpetrators were in face Boko Haram. (Conflicting report: some sources have the attack occurring on 2 Oct, while other have the attack on 1 Oct, still others have differences in the causality count. )
NIG3983: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen shoot and kill 20 at a government housing complex before fleeing ion a boat in the Ngadabul River.
NIG3985: An unidentified man (unknown affiliation) detonates a bomb in a heavily populated area of the city, but causes no damage or harm. The individual was later arrested.
NIG3986: A traveler is attacked and nearly killed by ethnic Fulanis.
NIG3984: Unidentified gunmen shoot and kill two police officers. Boko Haram maintains a presence in the State, but they were not openly suspected here.
NIG3988: Suspected members of Boko Haram detonate an explosive targeting military patrol, causing one death and four injuries.
NIG3982: Several groups, including ASUU: Academic Staff Union of Universities, NLC and the national socialist movement gathered to under the umbrella group JAF to protest Nigerias woes on the 52nd university of independence.
NIG3987: Fifty children, dressed in green and white colors, in Lagos staged a peace walk to advocate for violence against women and children, as well as their peace and safety.
NIG3978: Suspected detonate a suicide style bomb near an Islamic school causing unknown causalities, though injures have been widely reported.
NIG3979: Unidentified gunmen kidnapped the Delta State Commissioner for Higher Education, Prof. Hope Eghagha, assumedly for ransom. During the operation, his orderly, a police sergeant, was killed in the crossfire while his driver reportedly sustained serious injury.
NIG3980: Security agents shot and killed two suspected members of Boko Haram as they attempted to carry out operations on a Christian church following an attack on an Islamic school in the same area.
NIG3976: Four people are killed when suspected members of Boko Haram open fire on guests of a wedding. At least one reported injury.
NIG3977: Boko Haram (actir not confirmed) shoot and kill two police officers along a road.
NIG3974: University students riot over the killing of a fellow student by a hit-and-run driver. Much of campus property destroyed, including cars and animals of the agricultural department.
NIG3971: One is killed when two armed men entered Lagos State University and opened fire on students. Two others injured.

NIG3970: Three protesting Lagos State University students are injured when police break up their demonstration against a delay in university payment.
NIG3969: Thousands of Shiite Muslims gather to denounce the US, UK and Israel following waves of protests around the region. No incidents of violence reported.
NIG3966: A suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber detonates a car suicide car bomb outside a Catholic Church, at least three killed, plus the bomber, scores injured. Some reports have the death count as high as five.
NIG3965: The Nigerian military kills 35 members of Boko Haram and makes sweeping arrests over two days in three neighbourhoods (not named) across the city.
NIG3967: The JTF raids a Boko Haram bomb factory, make 156 arrests of suspects, including a high profile leader of the group.
NIG3961: The JTF conducted two separate Boko Haram raids in different parts of the city. Four dead, three arrested.
NIG3963: The JTF killed four and arrested three suspected members of Boko Haram during two separate raid operations throughout the city.
NIG3964: Arrests: 32 suspected members of Boko Haram were arrested in a combined JTF/Police effort. The raids took place in several wards of the city over a six hour period.
NIG3960: Tens of thousands protest in Kano against a anti-Islam US film. The group chanted 'death to America, death to Israel and death to the enemies of Islam'.
NIG3962: Shiite Muslims in the Nigerian town of Katsina burned U.S., French and Israeli flags and a religious leader called for protests to continue until the makers of the film and cartoons are punished.
NIG3959: Youths of the surrounding communities of a oil flow station protest the companies handling of a recent oil spill in the area. After police maintain a presence near the protesters several of the youths engage the them with violence.
NIG3958: Four persons killed following a PDP inter party conflict over a candidate.
NIG3957: Boko Haram gunmen stormed a medical clinic, kill the medical directors son.
NIG3956: Thousands of Muslims, under the auspices of a pro-Iranian Shiite group, Islamic Movement, gather to burn US and Israeli flags and denouncing a US made anti-Islamic film, following the possible AQIM attack in Benghazi and other worldwide protests.
NIG3953: Soldiers shoot and kill two suspected Boko Haram commanders on the outskirts of the city.
NIG3954: Unidentified gunmen open fire on two police officers, killing them. along Afikpo Street
NIG3955: Hundreds of Bakassi youths gathered at the national assembly building to warn if nothing was done by the Federal Government before the October 10 deadline to reclaim the disputed oil-rich area, they would raise a terror group like Boko Haram in Cross River State.
NIG3952: Unidentified gunmen shot and killed the justice commissioner, Zannah Malam, in a small town outside of Maiduguri.
NIG3950: Unidentified persons kill four, injure nine and virtually destroy a small village in the early morning hours. It is possible the violence was driven by ethnic unrest.
NIG3951: Gunmen shot dead the acting Chairman of Maiha Local Government Council of Adamawa State, Lawan Datti. Reasons unknown.
NIG3947: Soldiers manning a checkpoint in northern Nigeria shot to death two ranking members of Boko Haram, including Abu Qaqa, a spokesman for the group.
NIG3948: A soldier and 13 members of suspected Boko Haram were killed during a shootout after an explosive was thrown into a military vehicle. Other reports have the death total at 10.
NIG3949: Members of the JTF killed one member of Boko Haram and arrested two others. Following the shootout the JTF recovered 36 large explosives from a den. The deceased was later learned to be an official in the organization.
NIG3945: Gunmen suspected of belonging to the Boko Haram Islamist sect late Sunday shot dead at least six people who were playing ludo game in northern Nigerian city of Bauchi. Conflicting reports have the death total at 5.
NIG3944: Gunmen kill a security officer and three members of his family. Authorities believe Boko Haram is responsible.
NIG3946: Residents of Iperu gather to protest the killing of a police officer in recent days.
NIG3943: A group of 2,000 university students gathered to protest reported sexual harassment of female students by some staff of the school.
NIG3941: Following the end of Fridays Jumaat prayers, large groups of Muslims gather in Zololo Junction for an anti-American/Israeli protest, in the wake of violence in Libya and Egypt. In response, soldiers told the demonstrating youths to refrain and stop the demonstration and disperse. But the warning was not heeded, forcing the soldiers to shoot sporadically into the air to disperse them. Security forces added further security to the cities of Kano and Kaduna, anticipating further protests.
NIG3939: Unidentified gunmen attacked the home of a member of the Federal House of Representatives (name withheld), killing a young boy in the process.
NIG3940: Ijaw youths attack a police station in violent protest over an attack by police on an ex-militant Ijaw commander earlier in the week.
NIG3937: Protests are held over the recent firing of Delta State Oil Producing Communities Development Commission (DESOPADEC) by the House of Assembly.
NIG3938: Employees of the states internal revenue service protest the non-payment of taxes by shop owners.
NIG3934: Following a gunfight, the JTF arrested six suspects of a recent kidnapping of a university lecturer.
NIG3935: Local government workers in Ekiti State protested against non-implementation of the new minimum wage in local government areas.
NIG3936: Employment of a university protest the non-payment of allowances.
NIG3933: Striking workers throw stones and raid the office of a university vice chancellor. The group was upset over the non-payment of allowances.
NIG3931: House Assembly aides protest unpaid salaries. The group numbered in twenty.
NIG3929: Military officials kill seven suspected members of Boko Haram at a military checkpoint. 13 others arrested. No casualty was recorded on the part of the soldiers
NIG3928: Unidentified gunmen disrupt a political meeting.
NIG3927: Boko Harams attacks on telecommunication offices continue, many buildings in the area set ablaze.
NIG3925: The Military's Operation Restore Order shoots and kills seven suspected members of Boko Haram and arrested 13 others during a raid operation.
NIG3926: Air Nigeria employees protest unpaid benefits at a major airport.
NIG3924: Boko Haram continuers their attacks on telecommunication offices.
NIG3922: A journalist for the Nigeria Guardian claims to have been attacked by police and security forces for taking photographs of a cabinet ministers car stuck in mud.
NIG3923: An attack on a JTF patrol results in a counterattack and the death of seven Boko Haram attackers. 13 others arrested.
NIG3912: Suspected Boko Haram attacked two buildings housing the Ministry of Religious Affairs and the states Pilgrims Welfare Commission (YPWC) located on Potiskum Road. There was no official confirmation of the casualty figures but hospital sources claimed that 16 bodies were brought to the facility by the police and the JTF. The attacked carried into the early hours of the following day.
NIG3915: Boko Haram attack several telecommunication offices in a small geographic area. No report of injury or death.
NIG3920: Boko Haram set ablaze a telecommunications office in a coordinated effort to destroy much of the areas infrastructure. Sources revealed that the assailants, who were about 10 in number, stormed the telecommunications office around 2a.m. Wednesday and chased away the security men on duty before setting the building on fire.
NIG3913: Property destruction: Men on motorbikes, believed to be Boko Haram, destroyed MTN and Airtel mobile phone telecommunication masts during the early morning hours.
NIG3914: Property destruction: Boko Haram attack several telecommunication offices in a small geographic area. No report of injury or death.
NIG3909: Men believed to be of Boko Haram attacked a home and killed four Igbos. It is unclear if the group was targeted because they were Igbos or if the attack was coincidental.
NIG3911: Boko Haram carries out a series of coordinated attacked on telecommunications facilities in several areas. One is injured at this location, while several others ran for safety following the blast.
NIG3910: Boko Haram carries out a series of coordinated attacked on telecommunications facilities in several areas. Two bombs failed to detonate in tow separate areas along Gombe road.
NIG3907: A group protests the planned destruction of a open-air market.
NIG3906: Unknown gunmen burnt the personal house of Damaturu local government PDP chairman Alhaji Audu
NIG3908: A local government secretary of Bama Council area of Borno state, and his friend, a university lecturer were shot dead by gunmen suspected to be Boko Haram in the same area where six people were shot and killed by the same group on Saturday.
NIG3905: Unidentified men attempt to attack three police vehicles with explosives, but are unsuccessful.
NIG3903: Suspected Boko Haram kills a man in Gwange Ward of the city.
NIG3904: Suspected Boko Haram kills a man in Ummarari Ward of the city.
NIG3902: Boko Haram members detonated a bomb in the Sabon neighbourhood of Gombe. No causalities confirmed.
NIG3901: Six are shot dead by suspected Boko Haram. The event may have occurred on 2nd September.
NIG3899: Weapons Seizure: A JTF raid on a suspected Boko Haram hideout recovers a large cache of weapons.
NIG3900: Gunmen suspected to be members of the Boko Haram, weekend, stormed New Marte, Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, where they killed a Police Sergeant (names withheld), and two civilians. The group also burnt a police headquarters and a local church.
NIG3896: A group of suspected Boko Haram ambushed a JTF patrol, though the counterattack killed all five attackers.
NIG3897: A JTF patrol is ambushed by members of Boko Haram. One officer was reported killed.
NIG3898: Suspected Boko Haram attacked a military checkpoint, kill an intelligence officer.
NIG3893: Suspected members of Boko Haram attempt to bomb a JTF patrol, but the device exploded prematurely destroying nearby shops. Members of the JTF react with gunfire costing five members of BH their lives.
NIG3894: Protesters demand the removal of the Naval Chief of Staff for the naval detention of a man.
NIG3895: A group of pensioners gathered on the grounds of their former employer to protest non-payment.
NIG3892: Suspected Boko Haram suicide bomber was killed as well as a passerby when his explosive detonated prematurely. The suspected target was members of the JTF.
NIG3891: Suspected Boko Haram detonated an explosive in the Gwange area of the city late in the afternoon. Sporadic gunshots were reported in the area soon after. There was a explosion earlier in the day elsewhere in the city.
NIG3890: Unidentified gunmen abduct a government official.
NIG3889: A group of armed men, believed to be Boko Haram, shoot and kill a police officer during a gun battle.
NIG3888: Unidentified gunmen invaded Okordia community in Yenagoa Local Government Area, Bayelsa State, and abducted a clan head, or traditional ruler at a local palace.
NIG3887: Unidentified gunmen follow a police officer into a Mosque, kill him.
NIG3886: Boko Haram gunmen (suspected) shoot and kill a Irish national working for a construction firm.
NIG3885: Fulani militiamen raid a village and, kill two Christian residents.
NIG3884: Two suspected assassins are killed in a police gun battle. The two are believed to be in connection with the death of a British national.
NIG3883: Lecturers gather at a university to protest to demand the release of a kidnapped colleague, who was taken by unknown men for a large ransom.
NIG3879: Boko Haram suspects attack a police station/prison and exchange gunfire. Reports of civilian injury or death, though numbers are unknown The gun battle lasted at least two hours according to witnesses.
NIG3880: Protesters gather after the state House Assembly did not swear in a recently elected official.
NIG3878: Boko Haram suspects open fire on separate mosques, killing two.
NIG3877: Boko Haram suspects attack a Christian church and a school. No report of injury or death. It is believed this group is the same group that attacked the police station elsewhere in the city.
NIG3876: Suspected Boko Haram militants disrupt a Eid-el-Fitr celebration, no report of death or injury.
NIG3874: A policeman was reportedly injured when suspected Boko Haram members fired at a military roadblock along Maiduguri Road, Kano, while the police stopped a violent confrontation between Boko Haram and some residents of the area. Many cars damaged.
NIG3875: After a suspected Boko Haram attack in their neighbourhood, a group of Christian youths seek revenge on their attackers. Police we able to foil most of the violence.
NIG3873: Two students are dead after an attack by Fulani Herdsmen on their village. Reports of women raped and houses burnt.
NIG3871: An unidentified gunman is killed after a three hour gun battle with police.
NIG3872: Protesters threatening violence stormed the premises of the State Oil Commission expressing grievances over alleged neglect by the commission. The group, mostly youths, armed with weapons, caused employees to flee.
NIG3866: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, attack a mosque and shot dead a member of the Borno Emirate Traditional Council (BETC), Zanna Kaselama.
NIG3867: Violence broke out at the Rivers State University of Science and Technology (RSUST) as 'hoodlums' attacked officials of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) opposed to the appointment of an acting vice chancellor.
NIG3868: During a Muslim celebration festival unknown persons bomb a police station. The blast injured one person and destroyed property.
NIG3864: Hundreds evacuate a downtown building after a bomb scare.
NIG3869: The NUJ holds a protest demonstration against recent violence on journalists. The demonstration was held in part in front of the governors home.
NIG3860: A Boko Haram suicide bomber killed himself and a civilian while wounding three others in an attack targeting a military vehicle. The members of the military were not harmed.
NIG3861: Military forces battle Boko Haram when they raid their hideout. 30 arrested.
NIG3863: A gun duel between Boko Haram and JTF security forces lasts two hours. One militant death reported, one soldier injured.
NIG3862: Local traders protested the demolition of their shops and structures by the State Government.
NIG3858: Three people were killed in a bomb blast on a northern Nigerian road leading to a mosque where a cleric had condemned the Islamist militant group Boko Haram. The ordinance was delivered on motorcycle.
NIG3859: Two suspected suicide bombers were killed by an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) while another person suspected to be a member of the group escaped with injuries. Their bomb was concealed in a camera case. The assailants were unknown, but it is likely they were members of Boko Haram. Some reports have the death count at three.
NIG3853: A gang known as the Area Boys attacks a journalist.
NIG3857: Six unidentified men attack journalists on a train.
NIG3855: The Joint Research and Allied Institutions Sector Union on Monday in Enugu embarked on a demonstration to protest the Federal Government's perceived failure to implement the agreement to improve the welfare of its members.
NIG3856: A physically challenged group protests neglect by the state government by barricading a road outside the capital city.
NIG3852: Gunmen, suspected to be members of Boko Haram attack a church in Gombe.
NIG3849: Joint Task Force (military force) killed 20 suspected Boko Haram members in a shootout as they raided their hideout in Maiduguri. Conflicting report: some accounts have this event occurring on the 13th of the month.
NIG3850: A JTF raid on two Boko Haram hideouts results in the death of two militants and the arrest of 30 others. Panicked residents flee the city in large numbers.
NIG3846: Weapons Seizure: Security forces raid a suspected Boko Haram hideout and recover a large cache of weapons.
NIG3848: Adherents to the CNPP protest a local election, believing it was fixed.
NIG3843: Unidentified gunmen attack a church, set it ablaze. Injuries, one death reported.
NIG3842: Suspected Boko Haram kill one member of a security forces and wound two others in a 'militant attack.'
NIG3845: Weapons Seizure: A team of the JTF raided a Boko Haram hideout, recovered weapons.
NIG3844: Over 40 lawyers in Asaba, the Delta state capital on Friday barricaded magistrates' courts to protest the abduction of a newly appointed judge, Justice Marcel Okoh. NIG3840: Suspected members of Boko Haram kill two police officers along a rural road.
NIG3839: Members and adherents of the BSDF declare their independence from Nigeria, believing the land of southeast Cross River State rightfully belongs to Cameroon. Upen their declaration the group launched a radio station.
NIG3835: Day two of rival cult clash.
NIG3834: Unknown assailants opened fire on a group of soldiers on patrol, sparking an exchange of fire that left two soldiers and two of the gunmen dead. It is unclear if the perpetrators have any connection to the church attackers the previous night.
NIG3836: Communal violence has occurred in Benue State with 10 persons killed and property worth millions of naira destroyed in Ojantele and Ijegwu communities in Otukpo and Obi local council areas.
NIG3838: Relatives of fallen police officers gather at police headquarters to protest the non-payment of pensions. Witnesses believe they numbered in the 1,000s.
NIG3830: Suspected Boko Hara(actor not confrimed) m opens fire on a crowded church during an evening service, at least 19 dead. Unknown injury number.
NIG3833: A commercial motorcyclist, popularly called okada rider was stabbed in the stomach by two hoodlums suspected to be Fulani herdsmen on the long bridge end of the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The attack did not appear to be criminal.
NIG3832: A confederation of bus drives protested the government imposition of a tax.
NIG3831: Rival 'cult' groups clash over the course of two days, causing at least tow deaths and other injuries.
NIG3828: A suicide bomber rammed his car into a military patrol in the northeastern Nigerian city of Damaturu, killing himself, six soldiers, and two civilians. Boko Haram was suspected and later claimed responsibility. Nine other were hospitalized.
NIG3829: Hundreds of Ogoni ethnics took to the streets at Ogale-Eleme, Rivers State to protest the non-implementation of a UN potable water campaign.

NIG3824: Unidentified gunmen attacked a oil vessel off the coast of Nigeria, killing two sailors and kidnapping four others. The victims were not citizens of Nigeria. Following the event the Nigerian military launched efforts to recover the victims.
NIG3825: Boko Haram attacks a second neighbourhood in Maiduguri.
NIG3826: Boko Haram attacks a third neighbourhood in Maiduguri.
NIG3827: Military forces raided a Boko Haram bomb factory in Kaduna.
NIG3822: A Muslim leader escaped a suicide attack in a mosque by suspected Boko Haram, who later claimed credit . 'The bomber, however, detonated the explosives and blew himself off, injuring two policemen and three civilians in the process,' a local official said.
NIG3820: Report of a bomb explosion at a church. However, conflicting accounts report no explosion at all.
NIG3821: Non-violent activity: Members of the Ogoni ethnic group declare their independence from Nigeria, calling on the UN to recognize them as a nation.
NIG3818: Boko Haram attacks a second police station into another area of the city, in an apparent coordinated attack.
NIG3819: Suspected Boko Haram simultaneously attacked two police stations in Gombe. 'They threw explosives and opened fire on the police post in central Gombe. Some of the policeman were inside while others were outside. The explosions were followed by gunfire. There was a shootout between the gunmen and policemen which lasted till 10 pm (2100 GMT),' a witness said. 'There were a lot of gunshots lasting for more than an hour. I cannot say if anybody was hurt or killed in the attack,' he continued.
NIG3816: Nigerian troops kill two members of Boko Haram new the country's border with Chad. The alleged insurgents were caught carrying rocket-propelled grenades, Kalashnikov rifles as well as other assorted ammunition and weaponry.
NIG3817: Defusal: Police discover and dispose of a explosive found at a school. Boko Haram is suspected, but there is no evidence to support the claim.

NIG3814: Explosions, including a suicide blast, rocked two police stations in Nigeria's northwestern city of Sokoto. Boko Haram later claims credit. Six killed, including civilians, 30 others injured. Other reports have the death count at four, others three.
NIG3812: Motorcycle gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, opened fire on the car of a senior Nigerian air force officer Sunday, killing the driver and an aide (both junior air force officers), but the senior officer was not inside the vehicle at the time. Two pedestrians were collateral damage.
NIG3813: The traditional ruler of an area is kidnapped by unknown men, later released.
NIG3811: Boko Haram attackers opened fire on Mosque worshippers. Three of the gunmen were shot by police who were present to protest the worshipers, while a fourth was killed when the explosive device he was carrying went off prematurely. Conflicting reports have the death count at five.
NIG3810: On motorcycles, suspected Boko Haram assassinate a senior member of the police forces while he ate at home. Three of the officers guests were also shot and killed.
NIG3809: Shortly after Boko Haram killed two Indian nationals in a factory, the JTF makes 26 BH arrests and kills two in a raid.
NIG3808: Suspected Boko Haram gunmen attack a police station. Three police reported killed.
NIG3806: Two Indian nationals are killed in a suspected Boko Haram attack on their factory. Other were injured.
NIG3805: Following the killing of two Indians, members of Boko Haram attacked a police station in a separate attack in a different area of the city. Two police and civilian shot dead in the attack.
NIG3807: Armed men of the Boko Haram sect attacked a police station, set it ablaze. It is suspected these are the same gunmen involved in the attack in rural Bauchi State
NIG3803: A prominent Christian leader is killed, his wife abducted, after unidentified gunmen storm their church.
NIG3804: A group of women barricaded a Shell petroleum facility in an event that lasted four hours. The group believed the company had not met their obligations to provide community amenities. The protesters also accused the company of environmental and social negligence.
NIG3800: Boko Haram kills a 10-yesr-old boy and wounds 10 others. The explosion occurred in the city's Tundunwadan Dan-iya area, a nightlife and pub district, a common target of Boko Haram, who later claimed credit for the blast.
NIG3801: Unidentified gunmen shot dead a Health Ministry worker after he was followed. The reasons for the killing are unknown. Witnesses claim the assailants did not leave the scene of the crime until they knew the victim was dead.
NIG3802: A gunman attacks a regional leader of MASSOB, but the leader escapes unharmed. It is unclear if this was an assassination attempt or a robbery.
NIG3799: Suspected Fulani herdsmen attacked the villages of Kai, Nyongon, Kachim, Kuffan, Begduk and Yokhol (all unincorporated) in Gashish District. There were no causalities.
NIG3797: During the planned demolition of a shanty town a police officer shot and killed an evicted resident and community leader.
NIG3798: A group of youths began throwing stones and other objects at an election official, accuse him of manipulating the voting process.
NIG3790: Gunmen, suspected to be of Boko Haram, target Ibo Christians in an open air market and kill four.
NIG3791: Youths of the MASSOB violently take over portions of a State Park, injuring 16 and causing damage.
NIG3795: Six are dead, including a police constable when gunmen on motorcycles attack a market area. Boko Haram is widely believed to be responsible.
NIG3796: Gunmen, suspected to be linked to Boko Haram attack a radio station and kill three. Sharada is a Kano neighbourhood south east of the downtown area.
NIG3794: Boko Haram attacks a JTF team along a road. Unknown causalities.
NIG3792: Members of the National Youth Service Corps protested the non-payment of allowances by the government.
NIG3793: Defusal: Police forces discover explosives outside a Catholic school in the capital and dispose of it before it is able to detonate.
NIG3786: A group of soldiers attacked a group of police with rocks and bottles after soldiers witnessed a police officer accosting the driver of a bus whom they believed was interrupting the flow of traffic.
NIG3784: One s dead after Fulani herdsmen clash with area natives over the alleged destruction of farming crops.
NIG3785: Non-violent activity: Hotel staff discover an unexploded bomb.
NIG3787: the National Union of Electricity Employees (NUEE) begin a multi-day protest of a Nigerian electrical companies merger with a Canadian counterpart.
NIG3789: Two communities protest a proposed merger into a new state fearing neglect by newly formed government.
NIG3781: An explosion outside a government building kills at least one. It is unknown is perpetrated the incident, though it is believed to be either Boko Haram or a Fulani group.
NIG3783: When a grenade is thrown at a Islamic school in a Jos suburb security agents respond with gunfire. One small boy was killed by the blast.
NIG3782: Members of the Onitsha Communal Militia attack two members of MASSOB, injuring them. The two were attacked for allegedly preventing them from collecting illegal levies from Onitsha traders.
NIG3779: Heavy gunfire reported in the Yobe State capital. Suspected Boko Haram members raid a police station. The organization later claims credit for the attack.
NIG3780: Defusal: Police forces discover and raid a bomb factory in a church.
NIG3776: A lynch mob attacks a suspected bike thief, kills him.
NIG3777: Gunmen, suspected to be Boko Haram, attack a small town outside Kaduna, kill one.
NIG3778: A bomb is detonated in a car outside a church during Sunday services, no causalities. Police arrest two suspects following the incident, who are believed to be involved in Boko Haram (not confirmed).
NIG3775: Unidentified gunmen attack and kill a Divisional Police Officer for unknown reasons.
NIG3774: A suicide bomber kills 10 in a Mosque near the Shehus palace. The Shehu is the top Islamic leader in the state. Six others injured. The bomber was a teenage boy, whom security experts believe was involved with Boko Haram.
NIG3773: Seven people wounded and many houses were destroyed when a neighboring community attacked another. The attack is believed to be motivated by the possession of land. The victims were of the Nkpor community.
NIG3770: Unknown gunmen kill four, injure one.
NIG3771: Reports of two small villages attacked by unknown people in Plateau State. Over 140 dead. The military disputes this claim.
NIG3769: A women's group of 2,000 protest the planned demolition of their houses. Reports of police violence.
NIG3768: Suspected members of Boko Haram attack and kill an Islamic cleric, Sheikh Ibrahim Majimi, at his home.
NIG3767: Fulani militiamen attacked a Brigadier General when his staff was changing a flat tire in the car he was travelling in. The militia group may have purposely blown the tire to set up the assassination.
NIG3765: Following Fulani attacks on Christian Birom villages, a mob of Birom and other Christian youths form to retaliate against members their attackers ethnic group or religion. Deaths caused, unclear number.
NIG3763: Muslim Fulani herdsmen (and/or Boko Haram) raided several villages. Here, a cemetery in Barkin Ladis area known as Maseh, at least 22 were killed in a raid, including two politicians. More than 200 people displaced among the villages. Later the Fulanis blame the military for the attacks.
NIG3766: Suspected members of Boko Haram attacked the residence of an Islamic cleric, Shehu of Borno, Alhaji Abubakar Umar Garbai El-Kanem, killing a resident of the palace as well as a trader in a nearby market.
NIG3764: State security forces push back against Fulani attacks, causing a two hour battle. Two police and 21 assailants killed. 14 civilians were listed among the dead, though it is not clear if the civilian death was caused by this fighting or the original Fulani attacks.
NIG3759: Fulani militants (and/or Boko Haram) raid six villages in the Barakin Ladi region (villages either unincorporated or not named) and kill at least 63. NIG3760: Fulani militias attack the town on Kushen in the Barakin Ladi area. 15 reported dead.
NIG3761: Fulani militias attack a Christian village early n the morning before attacking others in the area. 8 reported dead.
NIG3762: Fulani militants (and/or Boko Haram) raid several villages in the Riyom government area causing numerous deaths. Specific villages were not named. 58 were killed among to two areas. More than 200 displaced among the villages.
